data.title: Eco Cycles or How I Feel About Technology
data.author: Kvakes
data.article_summary: 文章《Eco Cycles or How I Feel About Technology》探讨了技术发展的周期性现象，称为“Eco循环”。每一项新技术的出现都带来初期的好处和兴奋，如传真机、电子邮件和汽车，但随着普及，这些技术逐渐成为负担。传真机被垃圾广告淹没，电子邮件泛滥成灾，汽车导致交通拥堵。文章指出，技术初期为早期采用者提供优势，但随着大众使用，逐渐失去魔力，变成需要管理的麻烦。这种循环不仅限于具体技术，还反映了更广泛的人类行为模式，如交通拥堵不仅是物流问题，更是心理和习惯问题。最终，技术虽然解放了我们，但也创造了新的管理和适应的挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术对社会及个人的影响，尤其是对注意力和生活方式的控制，以及是否可以或应该摆脱技术依赖。

不同观点：
• **A_Duck的观点**: 认为应用程序和网站设计者为了吸引用户100%的注意力而激励机制存在问题。默认应用程序本身无害，问题在于应用和内容设计的模式需要改变，以保留创新同时减少伤害。

• **CalRobert的观点**: 不同意A_Duck关于交通堵塞的观点，认为公共交通、自行车和良好城市设计能够解决交通问题，暗示技术并非唯一解决方案。

• **Kvakes的观点**: 认为技术并非全部都是为了解放人类，反映出对技术决定论的怀疑态度，强调技术对人类的影响具有两面性。

• **FollowingTheDao的观点**: 引用道家思想，认为技术带来的便利伴随着隐藏的代价，主张通过“ stepping out”来摆脱技术的束缚，回归简单生活。

• **Miraltar的观点**: 对技术像生命系统一样演化的观点感到有趣，但没有明确表态支持或反对技术决定论。

• **keybored的观点**: 批评硅谷技术专家用“技术决定论”来解释社会问题，认为这是逃避责任的做法。主张人们应正视并解决技术依赖问题，而非简单地归咎于技术或人性决定论。强调技术问题本质上是人为造成的，可以通过努力改善。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于技术是否不可避免地控制和影响人类生活（技术决定论），以及个人和社会是否能够或应该采取措施来减少技术带来的负面影响。
• keybored的评论进一步深入批评了技术行业对社会问题的推卸责任态度，并提出技术依赖是人为问题，需要人为解决。
• 评论中还涉及到城市设计、交通问题等具体案例，显示出对技术影响社会的广泛讨论。

43533595.article_content:
Eco Cycles or How I Feel About Technology
28 March 2025
Umberto Eco, the author of
The Name of the Rose
and
Foucault’s Pendulum
(my personal favorite), wasn’t just a brilliant scholar—he was also a bit of a geek. He once wrote an essay comparing Macs to Catholicism and PCs to Protestantism. He thought about technology a lot.
And he loved his fax machine. The ability to send manuscripts to his editor in minutes felt magical. At first.
But the magic didn’t last. Too many people had his number. The machine started spitting out unsolicited ads, junk, spam. Eventually, he just turned it off. What began as a miracle of speed became a firehose of noise.
That story isn’t unique to fax machines. It’s a familiar arc—one we’ve all lived through in different forms.
The Eco Cycle
Every major technology arrives with a promise, and for a while, it delivers. Early adopters ride the wave before anyone else even sees it coming. Imagine driving a car on an empty highway, going wherever you want. Or using the internet in the early 2000s—when it was chaotic, creative, and weird in the best way. If you were there, it felt like a revolution.
But then the crash comes.
Highways clog up. The internet becomes an ad engine. The comment section is a bloodbath, and you're constantly dodging phishing emails.
I call it the Eco Cycle: the lifecycle of a technology that starts as a powerful edge for early adopters and gradually decays into dysfunction as it goes mainstream.
The decay is slow. You don’t wake up one morning and realize the tool has turned on you. It happens drip by drip, feature by feature, until one day you’re not excited anymore—you’re just managing. You’re maintaining.
And by the time you see it, the system has already reshaped your habits, your expectations, your sense of what’s normal.
Technologies That Rode the Curve
Email was a breakthrough. It had the same kind of magic Eco experienced with his fax machine decades earlier. But the magic faded. The problem wasn’t just spam—it was volume. Faxes had friction. Email doesn’t. And when communication becomes nearly free, the floodgates open: low-effort check-ins, reply-all storms, endless CCs.
And email is just one tab. Now we juggle Slack, Teams, WhatsApp, DMs, Discord, LinkedIn messages, calendar invites, and comment threads. Communication didn’t scale insight—it scaled interruption.
Researchers at UC Irvine found that reducing email access lowers stress and improves focus. Other studies show that communication overload reduces cognitive performance—like missing a night of sleep. The effect is real, and measurable.
Email was a symbol of freedom—the ability to talk to anyone, anytime, from anywhere. It promised liberation from gatekeepers, postage, and distance.
Cars made the same promise fifty years ago. If you had one, you could go wherever you wanted, whenever you wanted. Mobility, autonomy, speed.
But the promise didn’t scale. Everyone got a car, and now we sit in traffic. Everyone got email, and now we drown in messages. The thing that once set you free becomes the thing you have to manage—not because it failed, but because it worked too well, for too many people, all at once.
Smartphones were supposed to keep us connected. Now they fragment our attention, mine our behavior, and demand our eyes every waking hour.
Fertilizers boosted crop yields, then wrecked the soil and poisoned the water. Antibiotics saved lives, then gave rise to drug-resistant superbugs. Cheap flights opened the world—and turned the most beautiful places into theme parks.
The pattern is always the same: what begins as a breakthrough becomes, with scale, a burden.
Why We’ll Never Solve Traffic Jams
I can't quite pinpoint the emotion I feel whenever I hear someone talk about solving traffic jams. My therapist thinks it’s because I’m generally not good at naming feelings, so there’s definitely work to do here. Anyhow, it's a strange cocktail: a mix of surprise, annoyance, disapproval of how tax money gets spent, disdain for meaningless conversations. There's quite a bit of ego—"I know better." But I’m working on it.
The thing is, we’ve tried. For decades. Bigger roads, smarter routing, new bypasses. And still, people sit in traffic for hours.
Because traffic isn’t a logistics problem. It’s a psychological one.
We had traffic jams with horses and carts. Then with Model Ts. Now with Teslas. We’ll have them with flying cars, or whatever Elon is cooking up next. Doesn’t matter.
When I lived in San Francisco, I couldn’t wrap my head around the fact that one of my coworkers spent four hours a day commuting. Four. Hours. And he didn’t mind. That’s the point. His tolerance for sitting in traffic was high enough that it was just… normal.
Give that same person a faster car, a smarter road, a flying drone-pod, and they won’t commute for less time. They’ll just live farther out. The metro stretches. The problem scales.
That’s why traffic never goes away. It’s not a bug. It’s baked into us.

data.title: James Webb Space Telescope Reveals That Most Galaxies Rotate Clockwise
data.author: instagraham
data.article_summary: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has observed that most spiral galaxies rotate in the same direction, with about two-thirds of 263 studied galaxies rotating clockwise. This challenges the idea of an isotropic universe, where galaxy rotations should be evenly distributed. Lior Shamir, the sole author of the study published in *Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society*, suggests this asymmetry could be due to the universe's origins in a rotational state, possibly supporting black hole cosmology—the theory that our universe exists within a black hole. Another explanation could be the Doppler shift effect, making galaxies rotating opposite to the Milky Way appear brighter and more detectable. Further research is needed to confirm these findings and their implications for cosmology, including potential recalibrations of distance measurements in the universe.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：宇宙中星系旋转方向的观察和解释

不同观点：
• **观察者相对性**：vincnetas指出，星系的旋转方向取决于观察者的位置，从不同角度观察，星系可以呈现顺时针或逆时针旋转。因此，观察到2/3的星系朝一个方向旋转可能只是因为我们所处的位置所致。

• **测量方法的质疑**：snitty质疑星系的旋转测量方法，提出如果从不同角度观察，星系旋转方向应如何确定。

• **宇宙在黑洞内的假设**：alenrozac和pushreply对宇宙存在于类似黑洞结构中的假设持开放态度，而damnitbuilds则对这一假设表示怀疑，并询问如果我们在黑洞内，奇点在哪里。

• 主要争议在于星系旋转方向的观察是否反映了宇宙的基本性质（如黑洞假设或测量错误）或仅仅是观察者视角所致。此外，关于Doppler效应是否能解释亮度变化的讨论也存在分歧。

43533306.article_content:
Spiral galaxies imaged by JWST that rotate in the same direction relative to the Milky Way (red) and in the opposite direction relative to the Milky Way (blue). The number of galaxies rotating in the opposite direction relative to the Milky Way as observed from Earth is far higher.
Shamir, Lior,
Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
, 2025 under
CC BY 4.0
NASA’s
James Webb Space Telescope
(JWST) launched into orbit around the sun in December 2021. Since then, it has been studying the history of our universe. Now, images of deep space from JWST’s Advanced Deep Extragalactic Survey (JADES) have revealed something puzzling: most galaxies rotate in the same direction.
About two-thirds of the 263 galaxies studied in a
paper
published February 17 in the
Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
rotate clockwise, while the other one-third rotate counterclockwise.
“The analysis of the galaxies was done by quantitative analysis of their shapes, but the difference is so obvious that any person looking at the image can see it,"
Lior Shamir
, a computer scientist from Kansas State University and sole author of the study, says in a
statement
. "There is no need for special skills or knowledge to see that the numbers are different. With the power of the James Webb Space Telescope, anyone can see it.”
The galaxies identified as rotating in the opposite direction relative to the Milky Way.
Shamir, Lior,
Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
, 2025 under
CC BY 4.0
The problem is that astronomers have long posited that galaxies should be evenly split between rotating in one direction or the other, astronomer
Dan Weisz
from the University of California, Berkeley, who was not involved with the study, wrote for
Astronomy
back in 2017. “This stems from the idea that we live in an ‘isotropic’ universe, which means that the universe looks roughly the same in every direction. By extension, galaxies shouldn’t have a preferred direction of spin from our perspective,” he added. According to Shamir, there are two strong potential explanations for this discrepancy.
One explanation is that the universe came into existence while in rotation. This theory would support what’s known as black hole cosmology: the hypothesis that our universe exists within a black hole that exists within another parent universe. In other words, black holes create universes within themselves, meaning that the black holes in our own universe also lead to other baby universes.
"A preferred axis in our universe, inherited by the axis of rotation of its parent black hole, might have influenced the rotation dynamics of galaxies, creating the observed clockwise-counterclockwise asymmetry,”
Nikodem Poplawski
, a theoretical physicist at the University of New Haven who was not involved in the study, tells
Space.com
’s Robert Lea. "The discovery by the JWST that galaxies rotate in a preferred direction would support the theory of black holes creating new universes, and I would be extremely excited if these findings are confirmed.”
The galaxies identified as rotating in the same direction relative to the Milky Way (counterclockwise).
Shamir, Lior,
Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
, 2025 under
CC BY 4.0
Another possible explanation involves the Milky Way’s rotation. Due to an effect called the
Doppler shift
, astronomers expect galaxies rotating opposite to the Milky Way’s motion to appear brighter, which could explain their overrepresentation in telescopic surveys.
“If that is indeed the case, we will need to re-calibrate our distance measurements for the deep universe,” Shamir explains in the statement. "The re-calibration of distance measurements can also explain several other unsolved questions in cosmology such as the differences in the
expansion rates of the universe
and the
large galaxies
that according to the existing distance measurements are expected to be older than the universe itself.”
It remains to be seen whether further research will confirm black hole cosmology or that astronomers have been measuring the universe’s expansion incorrectly—or perhaps something else entirely.

data.title: Technical Analysis – Improper Use of Private iOS APIs in Vietnamese Banking Apps
data.author: quyleanh
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了越南一些银行应用程序（如BIDV SmartBanking和Agribank Plus）不当使用iOS私有API（如SBSLaunchApplicationWithIdentifierAndURLAndLaunchOptions）检测用户设备上安装的其他应用程序（如TrollStore）。这种行为违反了苹果的政策，侵犯了用户隐私。技术分析显示，这些应用程序使用了名为“VNPay Runtime Protection”或“VNPShield”的机制，结合XOR加密来隐藏私有API使用。此类行为可能导致应用被苹果下架，影响数百万用户。文章澄清了BShield与此事的无关性，并强调其严格遵循合法检测方法，确保用户安全和合规性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：iOS应用在运行时加载动态库（.so/dylib）以及利用非公开API的问题

不同观点：
• **bradyriddle** 对iOS能够在运行时加载.so/dylib文件并调用其方法表示质疑，认为iOS应该对此类操作进行严格限制，并对iOS如何允许这种操作表示困惑。

• **quyleanh** 引用了开发者@opa334的言论，提到TrollStore以及@wh1te4ever发布的沙箱逃逸技术，暗示这些技术可能被用于绕过iOS的限制。

• **a012** 对银行应用使用非公开API来提供“保护”功能表示质疑，认为这种做法不恰当，尤其是在涉及用户安全的情况下。

• **musjleman** 认为将5000美元的漏洞赏金用于“枚举所有应用”的例子是不诚实的，因为这更像是检查某个特定应用是否通过非商店途径安装。同时，对将此类问题称为“零日漏洞”或“沙箱逃逸”表示不认同。

• **alephnerd** 指出，不仅仅是BIDV和Agribank，许多越南的银行应用都存在类似的“hacky fingerprinting”技术。这与近一两年的监管变化有关，要求使用银行应用进行身份指纹识别，并与新的生物识别技术推出相关联。

• **petesergeant** 总结了原文作者的立场，指出原文作者制作了一款用于检查手机上是否运行恶意应用的软件，并抱怨银行使用自己开发的系统进行类似的恶意应用检测，而这些银行的操作可能违反了Apple的规定，不如原文作者销售的软件安全。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于银行应用使用非公开API和动态加载库技术是否合理，以及这些操作是否违反了Apple的规定和用户安全原则。
• 对“零日漏洞”和“沙箱逃逸”等术语的使用存在争议，部分评论者认为这些术语过于夸张。
• 讨论中提到了具体的监管变化和技术实现（如TrollStore和沙箱逃逸），这些技术可能被用于绕过iOS的限制。

.

infosec.exchange
two days ago and later in a
Facebook post
on Vietnamse J2TEAM forum. The controversy quickly gained traction because such behavior suggests a violation of Apple’s policies and an invasion of user privacy.
The initial information in the Facebook post mentioned suspicions regarding our
BShield
Mobile Security solution, leading to a misunderstanding that inaccurately affected the reputation of BShield and Verichains.
Therefore, we conducted a thorough technical analysis of the mentioned bank apps
BIDV SmartBanking
(v5.2.62, updated on Mar 14, 2025) and

,
detailed in this write-up, which also examines implications for users and the banking apps.

TLDR;
The apps (BIDV SmartBanking and Agribank Plus) were reported of using the private iOS API
SBSLaunchApplicationWithIdentifierAndURLAndLaunchOptions
to detect TrollStore and other applications installed on users’ devices.
Technical analysis reveals that BIDV SmartBanking (v5.2.62, updated on Mar 14, 2025) and Agribank Plus (v5.1.8, updated on Mar 25, 2025), developed by VNPay, use commercial Mobile App Shield DexProtector/Licel and Dexguard/iXGuard, together with a self-developed code likely named “
VNPay Runtime Protection
” or “
VNPShield
”.
VNPay Runtime Protection employs a mechanism exploiting side-channel issue of iOS private API
SBSLaunchApplicationWithIdentifierAndURLAndLaunchOptions
to detect app presence on user iOS devices, combining with a very weak XOR encryption trying to hide the private API strings from scanning. This side-channel issue works on latest iOS versions on non-jailbroken device. According to
Apple Security Bounty Program
,  this issue likely falls under the category "Device attack via user-installed app – Unauthorized access to sensitive data", qualifying for a $5,000 bug bounty.
Exploiting private APIs to enumerate installed apps violates Apple App Store policies and pose a significant risk of App removal by Apple, potentially impacting millions of bank customers.
This policy violation has NO relation to
BShield
of Verichains.
The primary purpose of application shielding is to proactively protect banking applications against malicious apps on user devices, preventing account takeover, theft of money and personal data. From time to time, we are aware of various new detection methods, including certain tricks utilizing N-day exploits or private APIs. However, as an bank-grade Mobile App Protection solution protecting more than 100 millions users, BShield strictly uses only stable and legitimate detection techniques.  We do NOT use risky or dangerous methods, ensuring full compliance with store policies, prioritizing user and business security amid rising threats targeting banking apps.

• **quyleanh** 引用了开发者@opa334的言论，提到TrollStore以及@wh1te4ever发布的沙箱逃逸技术，暗示这些技术可能被用于绕过iOS的限制。

data.title: Show HN: NoteUX – Fast and minimalist note-taking app
data.author: ifrosted
data.article_summary: NoteUX是一款设计精美、功能实用的笔记应用，帮助用户快速捕捉和整理想法。其主要功能包括：多重草稿板，便于切换和管理不同笔记；暗黑模式，减少眼部疲劳；全屏模式，提供无干扰的写作体验；自动保存，确保笔记不丢失；实时字数统计，便于跟踪写作进度；以及笔记下载，支持离线使用。NoteUX界面简洁直观，适合追求高效和创造力的用户。用户可以轻松分享该应用，让更多人体验其简洁和无干扰的笔记功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于简约笔记应用程序的评价与需求

不同观点：
• [sashk] 提到该应用让他想起 IconFactory 的 Tot，并提供了相关链接，暗示可能存在设计上的相似性。
• [ahmedfromtunis] 表示目前缺少一个能替换新标签页为笔记空间的 Chrome 扩展，并提到以前使用的 Papier 扩展因不兼容 manifest V3 被移除，建议当前应用可以填补这一空白。
• [czhu12] 寻找支持本地存储和图像的笔记应用，并希望能够支持链接。
• [camflan] 直言该应用是 Tot 的抄袭版本，建议至少应注明灵感来源。
• [swah] 表达了对过多笔记应用的困扰，提到多个常用笔记应用，暗示用户在不同平台间切换的麻烦。

补充讨论：
• [numinix] 对应用提出多项建设性意见，包括对本地存储可靠性的担忧、隐私问题、用户体验改进（如字体和排版）、以及技术实现上的建议（如CSS文件的使用）。
• [ifrosted] 介绍了自己开发的 NoteUX，强调其简约和无干扰的特点，并请求反馈。
• [freetonik] 分享了自己最爱的笔记应用 nvALT 和其他极简解决方案，包括书签工具和自托管项目 Textpod。
• [roldie] 询问是否有现代的 Notational Velocity 替代品，强调其快速搜索功能。
• [mprovost] 幽默地提到使用 Unix 技巧将笔记重定向到 /dev/null。
• [egypturnash] 遇到 Safari 崩溃问题，对应用稳定性提出质疑。
• [qoez] 提到开发者间的竞争，认为在更高层次上仍有创新空间。
• [NoSalt] 分享了自己的类似项目 Ephemeranote，寻求反馈。
• [RandomBacon] 认为该作品更像网站而非应用，并推荐了一款安卓应用。
• [dlbucci] 在 iPhone SE 3 的 Firefox 上遇到无法输入的问题，指出兼容性问题。

争议焦点：
• 该应用是否过度借鉴 IconFactory 的 Tot（[camflan] 提出的抄袭指控与 [sashk] 的联想形成讨论）。
• 不同用户对简约笔记应用的功能需求和设计偏好存在差异，例如对隐私、设计美观、技术实现等的不同看法。
• 应用的跨平台兼容性和稳定性受到质疑，特别是不同浏览器和设备上的使用体验。

data.title: ToS;DR
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了网络服务条款中的常见问题，指出用户常常未经仔细阅读便同意这些条款，而其中包含许多不利于用户的隐私和数据处理条款。文章评析了多个知名网站，如Facebook、Amazon、Reddit、YouTube等，揭示它们在数据存储、跟踪用户、修改条款和删除内容等方面的做法。多数网站被评为"Grade E"，因其允许在未经用户同意的情况下使用第三方 cookies、修改服务条款、追踪用户行为，甚至在无理由情况下删除用户账户或内容。文章呼吁关注这些不合理条款，并倡导用户和企业共同改善这一状况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对服务条款（ToS）的理解和评价

不同观点：
• amichal认为ToS文件常常自相矛盾，难以解析。他引用了ToSdr.org上的例子，显示出同一服务在不同条款中的不一致性，令用户困惑。
• timcobb建议根据公司类型标准化ToS要求，认为某些条款对特定类型的公司是合理的，例如PayPal需要用户提供身份信息。
• serbuvlad对ToS评级系统的标准提出疑问，指出Wikipedia、Tor和DuckDuckGo等网站在评级上的不一致性。
• amelius提出用户应能在浏览器中自定义法律条款，使协议成为双向的，而非仅由公司单方面制定。
• synecdoche批评ToS通常由法律专家撰写，语言晦涩难懂，建议除非用通俗语言撰写，否则ToS应被视为非法。
• bsimpson以个人经历说明，即使是父母也常教导孩子在安装软件时直接点击同意，显示出用户普遍对ToS的忽视。
• cluckindan对某些网站（如Facebook和YouTube）能够查看用户浏览器历史的功能表示不解。
• ColinEberhardt称赞ToSdr.org的想法，但指出网站在处理垃圾评论方面存在问题。
• j_bum和woadwarrior01分别提到希望看到某些特定服务（Kagi和FreeOutput）的ToS评级。
• butz和osm3000质疑Tor浏览器为何获得C等级，尽管其条款评价全为正面。
• jameslk认为使用LLM可以帮助用户更好地理解ToS内容，提出这是对盲目接受条款的一种改进。
• piokoch对Wikipedia使用跟踪像素、浏览器指纹等技术表示不满，认为这与其非营利性质不符。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到ToS评级系统的不一致性和疑惑，特别是对不同网站在评级上的差异。
• 有争议的焦点包括ToS语言的难以理解以及如何改进（如通过LLM技术或法律规定），以及对特定网站在隐私保护上的实际操作与用户期望之间的矛盾。
• 用户普遍对ToS感到困惑和不满，认为当前的条款制定和展示方式对普通用户不友好。

• ColinEberhardt称赞ToSdr.org的想法，但指出网站在处理垃圾评论方面存在问题。
• j_bum和woadwarrior01分别提到希望看到某些特定服务（Kagi和FreeOutput）的ToS评级。
• butz和osm3000质疑Tor浏览器为何获得C等级，尽管其条款评价全为正面。
• jameslk认为使用LLM可以帮助用户更好地理解ToS内容，提出这是对盲目接受条款的一种改进。
• piokoch对Wikipedia使用跟踪像素、浏览器指纹等技术表示不满，认为这与其非营利性质不符。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到ToS评级系统的不一致性和疑惑，特别是对不同网站在评级上的差异。
• 有争议的焦点包括ToS语言的难以理解以及如何改进（如通过LLM技术或法律规定），以及对特定网站在隐私保护上的实际操作与用户期望之间的矛盾。
• 用户普遍对ToS感到困惑和不满，认为当前的条款制定和展示方式对普通用户不友好。

data.title: The Egg (By Andy Weir)
data.author: jxmorris12
data.article_summary: 《蛋》是由安迪·威尔创作的短篇小说，讲述了一个男子在车祸去世后遇到自称是上帝的实体。男子关心他的家人，上帝告诉他家人会没事，并解释没有天堂或地狱，只有轮回。男子疑惑轮回的意义，上帝解释他的灵魂包含所有前世经验，每次轮回都是为了成长和成熟。男子惊讶地发现，所有人类其实都是他的不同化身，包括历史人物如林肯、希特勒和耶稣。最终，上帝揭示宇宙存在的意义是为了让这个男子通过不同生命体验和成熟，所有人类经历的善恶都是他自身的体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对《The Egg》故事及其哲学内涵的解读与反应

不同观点：
• A_D_E_P_T认为该故事呈现了一种悲观主义和决定论的视角，将存在视为一段孤独且预定的旅程，个体生命被视为可牺牲且道德模糊。这种观点强调了故事中的虚无主义色彩，并指出作者无意中创造了一个令人不安的哲学框架。

fine. Your kids will remember you as perfect in every way. They didnt have
time to grow contempt for you. Your wife will cry on the outside, but will be

consolation, shell feel very guilty for feeling relieved.

now? Do I go to heaven or hell or something?
Neither, I said. Youll be
reincarnated.

through the void. Where are we going?

from somewhere. Somewhere else. And there are others like me. I know youll

meaning of life, the reason I made this whole universe, is for you to mature.
You mean mankind? You want us to
mature?
No, just you. I made this whole
universe for you. With each new life you grow and mature and become a larger

There is no one else, I said.
In this universe, theres just you and me.

of you.

everyone
!?

with a congratulatory slap on the back.

lived?

too, I added.

him.

data.title: Bell Labs Holmdel Complex
data.author: lordleft
data.article_summary: 贝尔实验室霍姆德尔综合大楼位于新泽西州霍姆德尔镇，是一座由著名建筑师埃罗·萨里宁设计的中世纪现代风格建筑，于1962年建成。该设施作为贝尔实验室的研究与开发中心运营了44年，高峰期有超过6000名研究人员，并见证了诺贝尔奖得主朱棣文在激光冷却方面的研究。由于公司重组，该建筑于2006年出售，并在2013年后由Somerset Development重新开发为多用途空间，名为Bell Works，专注于高科技初创公司。2017年，该建筑被列入国家历史名胜名录。此前，该地还因卡尔·央斯基发明射电天文学而闻名，并设有纪念碑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：贝尔实验室旧址及其在《Severance》剧中的使用，以及其历史和再利用问题。

不同观点：
• [samgranieri] 提到刚看了《Severance》并对剧中的Lumon建筑感兴趣，感觉像以前通勤去郊区办公园区。
• [jt-hill] 表示立刻认出了《Severance》中的中庭，并借机向妻子讲解了贝尔实验室的历史，尽管妻子并不感兴趣。
• [_fat_santa] 认为《Severance》利用这个建筑很棒，但也指出很多办公楼因为太大且用途单一而被闲置。
• [Zealotux] 提到有些人可能认出了这个建筑，并分享了一个关于该建筑的视频链接。
• [dave333] 对建筑周围的椭圆形道路设计感兴趣，认为其设计避免了T型路口和交通灯的需求，仅通过并道实现连续通行。
• [Zigurd] 分享了参观贝尔实验室的经历，描述了其在贝尔实验室辉煌时期和AT&T解体后的不同状态，并对如此大的建筑能够被重新利用感到欣慰。
• [alexpotato] 回忆了贝尔实验室以前定期举办的公开讲座，并分享了自己高中时参加这些讲座的经历，特别提到一个关于语音识别的演示。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了贝尔实验室的历史意义，包括其在技术创新中的贡献和后来的衰落。
• 有人关注该建筑的再利用问题，特别是其规模过大可能导致利用困难。
• 对《Severance》剧中使用该建筑的反应不一，有人对建筑本身更感兴趣，而有人则对剧集本身感兴趣。
• 讨论中也提到了具体的技术演示和建筑设计的独特性，如椭圆形道路设计和语音识别技术。

Nvidia GPU roadmap confirms it: Moore’s Law is dead and buried
46
More silicon, more power, more pain for datacenter operators
Tobias Mann
Sat 29 Mar 2025
//
14:08 UTC
Comment
As Jensen Huang is fond of saying, Moore's Law is dead – and
at Nvidia GTC this month
, the GPU-slinger's chief exec let slip just how deep in the ground the computational scaling law really is.
Standing on stage, Huang revealed not just the chip designer's next-gen
Blackwell Ultra
processors, but a surprising amount of detail about its next two generations of accelerated computing platforms, including a 600kW rack scale system
packing 576 GPUs
. We also learned an upcoming GPU family, due to arrive in 2028, will be named after Richard Feynman. Surely you're joking!
It's not that unusual for chipmakers to tease their roadmaps from time to time, but we usually don't get this much information all at once. And that's because Nvidia is stuck. It's run into not just one roadblock but several. Worse, apart from throwing money at the problem, they're all largely out of Nvidia's control.
These challenges won't come as any great surprise to those paying attention. Distributed computing has always been a game of bottleneck whack-a-mole, and AI might just be the ultimate mole hunt.
It's all up and out from here
The first and most obvious of these challenges revolves around scaling compute.
Advancements in process technology have slowed to a crawl in recent years. While there are still knobs to turn, they're getting exponentially harder to budge.
Faced with these limitations, Nvidia's strategy is simple: scaling up the amount of silicon in each compute node as far as they can. Today, Nvidia's densest systems, or really racks, mesh 72 GPUs into a single compute domain using its high-speed 1.8TB/s NVLink fabric. Eight or more of these racks are then stitched together using InfiniBand or Ethernet to achieve the desired compute and memory capacity.
At GTC, Nvidia
revealed
its intention to boost this to 144 and eventually 576 GPUs per rack. However, scaling up isn't limited to racks; it's also happening on the chip package.
This became obvious with the
launch
of Nvidia's Blackwell accelerators a year ago. The chips boasted 5x the performance uplift over Hopper, which sounded great until you realized it needed twice the die count, a new 4-bit datatype, and 500 watts more power to do it.
The reality was, normalized to FP16, Nvidia's top-specced Blackwell dies are only about 1.25x faster than a GH100 at 1,250 dense teraFLOPS versus 989 — there just happened to be two of them.
By 2027 Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expects racks to surge to 600kW with the debut of the Rubin Ultra NVL576 - Click to enlarge
We don't yet know what process tech Nvidia plans to use for its next-gen chips, but what we do know is that Rubin Ultra will continue this trend, jumping from two reticle limited dies to four. Even with the roughly 20 percent increase in efficiency, Huang expects to get out of TSMC 2nm, that's still going to be one hot package.
It's not just compute either; it's memory too. The eagle eyed among you might have noticed a rather sizable jump in capacity and bandwidth between Rubin to Rubin Ultra — 288GB per package versus 1TB. Roughly half of this comes from faster, higher capacity memory modules, but the other half comes from a doubling the amount of silicon dedicated to memory from eight modules on Blackwell and Rubin to 16 on Rubin Ultra.
Higher capacity means Nvidia can cram more model parameters, around 2 trillion at FP4, into a single package or 500 billion per "GPU" since they're counting individual dies now instead of sockets. HBM4e also looks to effectively double the memory bandwidth over HBM3e. Bandwidth is expected to jump from around 4TB/s per Blackwell die today to around 8TB/s on Rubin Ultra.
Unfortunately, short of a major breakthrough in process tech, it's likely future Nvidia GPU packages could pack on even more silicon.
The good news is that process advancements aren't the only way to scale compute or memory. Generally speaking, dropping from say 16-bit to 8-bit precision effectively doubles the throughput while also halving the memory requirements of a given model. The problem is Nvidia is running out of bits to drop to juice its performance gains. From Hopper to Blackwell, Nvidia dropped four bits, doubled the silicon, and claimed a 5x floating point gain.
But below four-bit precision, LLM inference gets pretty rough, with rapidly climbing perplexity scores. That said, there's some interesting research being done around super low precision quantization, as low as 1.58 bits while maintaining accuracy.
Not that reduced precision isn't the only way to pick up FLOPS. You can also dedicate less die area to higher precision datatypes that AI workloads don't need.
We saw this with Blackwell Ultra. Ian Buck, VP of Accelerated Computing business unit at Nvidia, told us in an interview they actually nerfed the chip's double precision (FP64) t

data.title: Don't write clean code, write CRISP code
data.author: chautumn
data.article_summary: John Arundel在文章中提出，不应仅追求“干净代码”，而应追求CRISP代码，即**正确性（Correct）**、**可读性（Readable）**、**可测试性（Testable）**、**简洁性（Simple）**和**谦逊态度（Pessimistic）**。他指出，正确性是代码的首要属性，即便代码具备其他优点，若不正确则毫无意义。可读性同样重要，应优先于性能等其他因素。代码应易于测试，测试本身也需仔细审查以确保其有效性。简洁性意味着去除一切让代码难以理解的部分。最后，程序员应保持谦逊，假设代码有错误并积极寻找和修复问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对代码质量标准及其定义的讨论

不同观点：
• [cedilla] 认为原文没有提供明确的、可操作的建议，并质疑原文的主旨。他指出，虽然反对复杂且难以理解的代码是有道理的，但“clean code”的概念已经涵盖了这一点，且比CRISP更加广为人知。同时，他认为“clean code”虽然定义不明确，但CRISP也同样存在定义不清的问题。他还反驳了原文的开篇论点，指出没有人会故意写错误、难以理解、个性化、复杂或低效的代码。

• [lioeters] 支持CRISP概念，并给出了简要解释：正确的（Correct）、可读的（Readable）、符合语言习惯的（Idiomatic）、简单的（Simple）以及高效的（Performant）。他通过这几个词来定义好的代码标准，似乎认为CRISP比“clean code”更具体和有指导意义。

补充讨论：
• [cedilla] 对CRISP和“clean code”的关系提出了对比，暗示两者在定义上都有不足之处，但他更倾向于使用“clean code”作为指导原则。
• [lioeters] 用简洁的语言为CRISP提供了具体的定义，试图澄清其含义并表明其优越性。
• 争议焦点在于“clean code”与CRISP哪一个更具指导意义以及更清晰。此外，关于代码质量标准的定义和实用性也是讨论的核心。

Don't write clean code, write CRISP code
John Arundel
I’m sure we’re all in favour of “clean code”, but it’s one of those
motherhood-and-apple-pie things that no one can reasonably disagree
with. Who wants to write
dirty
code, unless maybe it’s for a
porn site?
The problem, of course, is that few of us can agree on what “clean
code”
means
, and how to get there. A rule like “methods should
only do one thing”, looks great on a T-shirt, but it’s not so easy to
apply in practice. What counts as “one thing”?
Over a lifetime of programming that
began with a ZX81
and hasn’t
quite ended yet, I’ve found a few
principles
enduringly useful.
Principles are more flexible than rules, and might be more widely
applicable. So here are my five rules for CRISP code in Go: they’re not
necessarily in order of importance, except for the first one, but it
makes a nice backronym.
Correct
Your code may have lots of other wonderful things to be said for it,
but if it’s not
correct
, they don’t really matter. And, indeed,
if we’re willing to give up correctness, we can presumably obtain any
other attribute fairly easily.
It might seem obvious and not worth saying, but if incorrect code
exists, and I think it does, then surely it
is
worth saying,
because apparently someone didn’t get the memo.
What does it mean for code to be correct, actually? The
straightforward answer is “it does what the writer intended”, but even
that’s not quite right, because I might have
intended
the wrong
thing!
For example, I might write a prime number generator while labouring
under the erroneous impression that all odd numbers are prime. In this
case, my code might produce the odd integers, as I requested, but still
not be correct.
A good suite of
tests
, again like
apple pie, is something just about everyone would love to have, even if
they don’t always feel like putting in the necessary labour. And tests
are a necessary, though not sufficient, part of any good program. No
doubt there are some correct programs that don’t have tests, but who
knows which ones they are?
A well-written test expresses
what the
programmer thinks the code should do
under a given set of
circumstances, and running it should give us a certain level of
confidence about whether it actually does or not. Tests themselves can
be incorrect, though.
This is one reason why we need to be very suspicious and sceptical of
any given test. What does it look like it says? Does it
actually
say that? Is it the right thing to say? If it verifies
the program’s result against some expected result, is the
expectation
correct?
If the test claims to cover some particular section of code, does it
actually
test
the behaviour of that code in all important ways,
or does it merely cause it to be executed?
Not having tests is a terrible situation to be in, but it’s actually
slightly preferable to having tests that don’t work. A malfunctioning or
insufficient test may give us false confidence in code that also happens
to be incorrect.
Therefore, once you’ve written your tests, read them all again
extremely carefully, with an adversarial eye. Programmers are incurable
optimists: we always think our code will work, despite much evidence to
the contrary. Instead, we should assume that if there can
be
a
bug, then there
is
a bug.
Humility
isn’t a virtue often associated
with software engineers, but it’s certainly something that good test
writers know all about.
Even the most thoroughly tested code should not be assumed to be
correct. It should be assumed to be incorrect. It almost certainly
is.
Readable
Again, this might sound like something that doesn’t need saying:
who’s arguing for
unreadable
code? Not me, but there seems to
be a lot of it around, all the same. It’s not that anyone deliberately
sets out to write unreadable code, of course; it just ends up that way
because we mistakenly prioritise other virtues over readability.
Performance is one such virtue, and there are cases where performance
genuinely matters.
Not as many as you might
think
, though: computers are pretty fast these days, and since most
of what they do is in the service of us humans, they can usually afford
to take their time about it.
So, while readability isn’t
quite
as important as
correctness, it’s more important than anything else. Readability, as
Churchill said of courage, is rightly esteemed the first of qualities,
because it is the quality which guarantees all others.
What is it that
makes
code readable, or not? I don’t think
readability is something that you can
add
to your code: I think
it’s what you’re left with when you’ve taken
away
all the
things that make it hard to understand.
For example, a poorly-chosen variable name can put a bump in the
reader’s path. Using different names for the same thing, or the same
name for different things, is confusing. An unnecessary function call,
added purely to satisfy some
rule
like
“methods should be less than 10 lines”, breaks the reader’s flow.

• [cedilla] 认为原文没有提供明确的、可操作的建议，并质疑原文的主旨。他指出，虽然反对复杂且难以理解的代码是有道理的，但“clean code”的概念已经涵盖了这一点，且比CRISP更加广为人知。同时，他认为“clean code”虽然定义不明确，但CRISP也同样存在定义不清的问题。他还反驳了原文的开篇论点，指出没有人会故意写错误、难以理解、个性化、复杂或低效的代码。

• [lioeters] 支持CRISP概念，并给出了简要解释：正确的（Correct）、可读的（Readable）、符合语言习惯的（Idiomatic）、简单的（Simple）以及高效的（Performant）。他通过这几个词来定义好的代码标准，似乎认为CRISP比“clean code”更具体和有指导意义。

补充讨论：
• [cedilla] 对CRISP和“clean code”的关系提出了对比，暗示两者在定义上都有不足之处，但他更倾向于使用“clean code”作为指导原则。
• [lioeters] 用简洁的语言为CRISP提供了具体的定义，试图澄清其含义并表明其优越性。
• 争议焦点在于“clean code”与CRISP哪一个更具指导意义以及更清晰。此外，关于代码质量标准的定义和实用性也是讨论的核心。

43533556.article_content:
300+ Miles, One Charge, Supported by the Sun’s Rays
Aptera just completed its first-ever solar-supported road trip—driving over 300 miles on a single charge and proving that a solar EV isn’t just a concept for the future, but a real-world solution ready for the present.
Our Co-CEO Steve Fambro, along with a small crew, took Aptera’s production-intent vehicle on a road trip through the American Southwest. They started early in the snowy mountain town of Flagstaff, Arizona, where the vehicle was already pulling in 300 watts of solar energy before the day even began.
The route followed a stretch of historic Route 66—quiet roads, breathtaking scenery, and a test bed for a vehicle built to thrive independently. “It’s kind of the path not really taken,” Steve shared. “And that’s one of the reasons we wanted to do it this way.”
From Flagstaff to Hackberry, through Kingman and down to sunny Lake Havasu, Aptera performed with quiet confidence. Even on an overcast day, the team saw over 545 watts of solar input. That means more time exploring and less time searching for chargers.
During its 300+ mile journey, the vehicle handled every condition thrown at it: mountain passes, 18-wheelers, potholes, desert winds, highways, and winding country roads.
“The panoramic windshield gives you this incredible view of the landscape,” Steve said, describing the drive. “It’s like a big picture window into the future.”
The final stretch took the team back into California, where they reflected on the journey, the data, and the excited reactions from drivers who caught a glimpse of the vehicle on the road. “Almost everyone we passed had their phones out filming us,” Steve laughed. “It’s clear that Aptera’s design stops traffic—without needing to stop for a charge.”
This trip marks a huge milestone for Aptera, not only in validating our systems in real-world conditions but in showing what’s possible when you rethink transportation from the ground up. With every mile driven by our production-intent vehicles, we’re one step closer to a future where every journey is powered by the sun.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：法国政治家勒庞被判刑及禁止参选所引发的法律与政治争议

不同观点：
• [rsynnott的观点] 认为新闻报道可能忽略了重点，指出克里姆林宫发言人Peskov对民主规范的评论具有讽刺意味，因为允许政治家因其特殊身份而免于犯罪处罚并不符合常理。同时，对意大利副总理萨尔维尼将勒庞的判决视为欧盟对极右翼的宣战这一言论表示质疑，指出欧盟并不控制法国法院。
  
• [lloeki的观点] 强调法国"一审"判决可以上诉，而上诉具有中止效力，但此案中的五年不得参选的判决具有临时执行条款，这意味着上诉不会中止执行，这一细节引发了关于2027年总统选举的激烈争论。

• [Georgelemental的观点] 将勒庞的判决与近期罗马尼亚和土耳其的情况相提并论，认为这是北约国家取消民主的又一例证。

补充讨论：
• 关于判决的立即执行与政治影响的讨论：lloeki指出了法律程序中的细节，尤其是临时执行条款对政治局势的潜在影响，这与rsynnott对政治言论的质疑形成对照。
• 对欧盟与法国司法关系的质疑：rsynnott对萨尔维尼言论的批评揭示了对欧盟在法国司法体系中角色的误解或政治化解释。
• 国际视角下的民主倒退：Georgelemental从国际政治的角度，将法国的案件与罗马尼亚和土耳其的民主状况联系起来，暗示一种更广泛的民主倒退趋势。

争议的焦点：
• 法国法院对勒庞的判决及其立即执行的法律依据和政治影响。
• 欧盟在法国司法体系中的角色及其在政治言论中的被解读方式。

data.title: Kalua: An OpenWrt extension for building large mesh-networks
data.author: namanyayg
data.article_summary: "Kalua" 是一个基于 OpenWRT 的硬件无关扩展工具，使用 POSIX shell 编写，用于搭建、监控和管理大型 WiFi 网格网络。它支持多地点网络部署，包含计费、 captive portal、web 登录、数据保留以及第七层/第八层QoS等功能。项目提供了详细的构建和定制指南，用户可以通过脚本自动下载和构建 OpenWRT 及其相关组件。主要步骤包括克隆项目仓库、创建构建环境、选择硬件和用例，然后执行构建脚本以生成固件。项目文档和支持社区资源丰富，便于用户快速上手。

Key Points
Economic growth in the first quarter was just 0.3%, according to CNBC's Rapid Update which tallied the forecasts of 14 economists.
The survey also shows Core PCE inflation will remain stuck at around 2.9% for most of the year.
The dour new forecasts come as the decline in consumer and business sentiment from the emerging trade war is showing up in real economic activity.
U.S. President Donald Trump speaks to members of the media aboard Air Force One before landing in West Palm Beach, Florida, U.S., March 28, 2025.
Kevin Lamarque | Reuters
Policy uncertainty and new sweeping tariffs from the Trump administration are combining to create a stagflationary outlook for the U.S. economy in the latest CNBC Rapid Update.
The Rapid Update, averaging forecasts from 14 economists for GDP and inflation, sees first quarter growth registering an anemic 0.3% compared with the 2.3% reported in the fourth quarter of 2024. It would be the weakest growth since 2022 as the economy emerged from the pandemic.
Core PCE inflation, meanwhile, the Fed's preferred inflation indicator, will remain stuck at around 2.9% for most of the year before resuming its decline in the fourth quarter.
Behind the dour GDP forecasts is new evidence that the decline in consumer and business sentiment is showing up in real economic activity. The Commerce Department on Friday reported that real, or inflation-adjusted consumer spending in February rose just 0.1%, after a decline of -0.6% in January. Action Economics dropped its outlook for spending growth to just 0.2% in this quarter from 4% in the fourth quarter.
Zoom In Icon
Arrows pointing outwards
"Signs of slowing in hard activity data are becoming more convincing, following an earlier worsening in sentiment," wrote Barclays over the weekend.
Another factor: a surge of imports (which subtract from GDP) that appear to have poured into the U.S. ahead of tariffs.
The good news is the import effect should abate and only two of the 12 economists surveyed see negative growth in Q1. None forecast consecutive quarters of economic contraction. Oxford Economics, which has the lowest Q1 estimate at -1.6%, expects a continued drag from imports but sees second quarter GDP rebounding to 1.9%, because those imports will eventually end up boosting growth when they are counted in inventory or sales measures.
Recession risks rising
On average, most economists forecast a gradual rebound, with second quarter GDP averaging 1.4%, third quarter at 1.6% and the final quarter of the year rising to 2%.
The danger is an economy with anemic growth of just 0.3% could easily slip into negative territory. And, with new tariffs set to come this week, not everyone is so sure about a rebound.
"While our baseline doesn't show a decline in real GDP, given the mounting global trade war and DOGE cuts to jobs and funding, there is a good chance GDP will decline in the first and even the second quarters of this year," said Mark Zandi of Moody's Analytics. "And a recession will be likely if the president doesn't begin backtracking on the tariffs by the third quarter."
Moody's looks for anemic Q1 growth of just 0.4% that rebounds to 1.6% by year end, which is still modestly below trend.
Zoom In Icon
Arrows pointing outwards
Stubborn inflation will complicate the Fed's ability to respond to flagging growth. Core PCE is expected at 2.8% this quarter, rising to 3% next quarter and staying roughly at that level until in drops to 2.6% a year from now.
While the market looks to be banking on rate cuts, the Fed could find them difficult to justify until inflation begins falling more convincingly at the end of the year.

data.title: OSS-SEC: Three bypasses of Ubuntu's unprivileged user namespace restrictions
data.author: birdculture
data.article_summary:
Qualys 安全咨询报告披露了三个绕过 Ubuntu 非特权用户命名空间限制的方法，这些方法可能被本地攻击者利用来获取命名空间内的完整管理员权限，从而利用内核漏洞。具体绕过方法包括：

1. 使用默认安装的 `aa-exec` 工具切换到允许创建用户命名空间的 AppArmor 配置文件。
2. 使用默认安装的 `busybox` shell，其配置文件允许创建具有完整权限的用户命名空间。
3. 利用 `LD_PRELOAD` 加载一个默认配置允许创建用户命名空间的程序（如 `nautilus`）。

这些绕过方法仅影响命名空间内部权限，而不影响主机系统。Ubuntu 24.04 默认启用了对非特权用户命名空间的限制，但这些绕过方法暴露了潜在的安全问题。详细信息可参考 Ubuntu 官方帖子。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux安全机制中的潜在问题及其影响

不同观点：
• [o11c] 认为这并不是一个直接的漏洞，需要有内核的 `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` 权限才能进行恶意操作。同时提到，很多安全工具在处理多进程解释器时表现不佳，但他并不认为这是严重的漏洞。

• [eqvinox] 认为尽管这不是一个严重的漏洞，但仍然是安全层的失败。他指出，即使这不是一个大的安全 breach，但仍然不理想，尤其是人们依赖这些安全特性时。他认为，虽然这不是大问题，但安全特性中的这种漏洞还是值得注意的。

• [quotemstr] 强调未授权的用户命名空间本身不是一个安全漏洞。他认为 Ubuntu 禁用此功能的决策是短视的，并指出移除该功能会使得良好行为的非特权程序难以设置用户空间沙箱。他主张修复内核漏洞，而不是随机地移除有用的功能。

• [j45] 关注该问题是否仅限于 Ubuntu，还是也可能影响 Debian 等其他系统。这表明讨论点可能涉及不同 Linux 发行版之间的安全策略差异。

• [mjevans] 质疑如果没有 AppArmor 的"加持"，标准的 Linux 权限或容器组是否足以防止此类问题。他似乎在探讨 AppArmor 配置文件是否在某种程度上加剧了此问题。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于该问题是否构成真正的安全漏洞，以及各发行版（如 Ubuntu 和 Debian）如何处理相关安全策略。
- 有人认为这是安全层的失败，即使不严重，也应引起重视；其他人则认为 Ubuntu 禁用某些功能的决策是不恰当的，应该直接修复内核漏洞。
- 不同发行版间的处理方式差异也被提及，表明这可能是一个更广泛的生态系统问题。

43517734.article_content:
oss-sec
mailing list archives
By Date
By Thread
Three bypasses of Ubuntu's unprivileged user namespace restrictions
From
: Qualys Security Advisory <qsa () qualys com>
Date
: Thu, 27 Mar 2025 17:44:15 +0000
Qualys Security Advisory
Three bypasses of Ubuntu's unprivileged user namespace restrictions
========================================================================
Contents
========================================================================
Summary
Bypass via aa-exec
Bypass via busybox
Bypass via LD_PRELOAD
Acknowledgments
Timeline (advisory sent to the Ubuntu Security Team on January 15, 2025)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Prologue, from
https://grsecurity.net/10_years_of_linux_security.pdf:
+ February 2013 (v3.8) - Unprivileged User Namespace support added
- Greatly increased kernel attack surface, exposed many interfaces
that previously saw little security scrutiny
+ Attack surface exposed by unprivileged user namespaces isn't
decreasing anytime soon
- Even more functionality being exposed
------------------------------------------------------------------------
========================================================================
Summary
========================================================================
Ubuntu 23.10 introduced unprivileged user namespace restrictions (the
sysctl kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns) and Ubuntu 24.04
enabled them by default. From Alex Murray's excellent blog post at
https://ubuntu.com/blog/whats-new-in-security-for-ubuntu-24-04-lts:
"Unprivileged user namespaces are a widely used feature of the Linux
kernel, providing additional security isolation for applications, and
are often employed as part of a sandbox environment. However, [...]
unprivileged user namespaces also expose additional attack surfaces
within the Linux kernel. There has been a long history of (ab)use of
unprivileged user namespaces to exploit various kernel
vulnerabilities.
For Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, the use of unprivileged user namespaces is then
allowed for all applications but access to any additional permissions
within the namespace are denied. This allows more applications to more
gracefully handle this default restriction whilst still protecting
against the abuse of user namespaces to gain access to additional
attack surfaces within the Linux kernel."
Unfortunately, we discovered three different bypasses of these
unprivileged user namespace restrictions; each bypass allows a local
attacker to create user namespaces with full administrator capabilities,
and therefore to still exploit vulnerabilities in kernel components that
require capabilities such as CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CAP_NET_ADMIN:
- An unprivileged local attacker can simply use the aa-exec tool (which
is installed by default on Ubuntu) to transition to one of the many
pre-configured AppArmor profiles that do allow the creation of user
namespaces with full capabilities (for example, the chrome, flatpak,
or trinity profile).
- An unprivileged local attacker can first execute a busybox shell,
which is installed by default on Ubuntu, and is one of the programs
whose pre-configured AppArmor profile does allow the creation of user
namespaces with full capabilities.
- An unprivileged local attacker can LD_PRELOAD a shell into one of the
programs whose pre-configured AppArmor profile does allow the creation
of user namespaces with full capabilities (for example, nautilus is
installed by default on Ubuntu Desktop).
Clarification: such a bypass allows an unprivileged user to obtain full
capabilities *inside* a namespace, not on the host outside a namespace;
for comparison, a bypass is not even needed on most Linux distributions,
because they allow unprivileged users to obtain full capabilities inside
namespaces by default (and therefore to exploit CAP_SYS_ADMIN kernel
vulnerabilities for example), without any restriction at all.
For more information on these bypasses and user namespace restrictions,
please refer to Ubuntu's post at:
https://discourse.ubuntu.com/t/understanding-apparmor-user-namespace-restriction
========================================================================
Bypass via aa-exec
========================================================================
Are we all just algorithms doing what we're supposed to do or can we
escape our programming?
-- Jude, The Matrix Resurrections
While working on needrestart, particularly on commit e17b564 ("core: fix
regression of false positives for processes running in chroot or mountns
(#317)"), we tried to experiment with user and mount namespaces, but to
our great surprise we were barred from creating them as an unprivileged
user on Ubuntu 24.04 (although kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone is
enabled by default):
------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ id
uid=1001(tiffany) gid=1001(tiffany) groups=1001(tiffany),100(users)
$ unshare -U -r -m /bin/sh
unshare: write failed /proc/self/uid_map: Operation no

data.title: Atop 2.11 heap problems
data.author: baggy_trough
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Openwall项目中ATOP工具的一个安全漏洞（CVE-2025-31160），该漏洞源于ATOP尝试连接一个未明确激活的'atopgpud'守护进程的TCP端口，可能导致堆问题和段错误。解决方案包括修改默认行为，使ATOP不再自动连接TCP端口，除非使用特定启动标志（-k），并改进字符串解析以避免问题。同时，对于其他可选来源如'netatop'，也需通过特定标志（-K）启用，以防止类似问题。文章还提供了漏洞的背景、影响及修复建议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕软件工具 "atop" 漏洞的发现、影响及设计问题的讨论

不同观点：
• **ianbutler** 认为他们的工具 Bismuth 成功找到了漏洞，并提供了重现脚本的 SHA 作为证明，详细描述了发现过程，并分享了技术报告链接。他确认了漏洞的发现并公开了相关信息。

• **geerlingguy** 指出，这个漏洞并没有之前帖子暗示的那么严重，原本期待的是供应链攻击级别的严重问题，但实际发现的问题相对轻微。

• **cullenking** 分享了自己过去使用 atop 时遇到的类似问题，指出 atop 在设计上可能因为需要挂钩到多个系统位置而产生意外的后果，但他并不认为这是开发者的错。

• **unsnap_biceps** 和 **Zardoz84** 都对 atop 使用 TCP 端口而不是 Unix socket 进行本地连接表示不满，认为这是一种不良设计，可能导致不必要的安全隐患。

• **Galanwe** 质疑漏洞的实际影响，认为如果需要本地权限才能利用该漏洞，那么其危害性相对较低，因为拥有本地权限的攻击者已经可以通过其他手段进行破坏。

• **yjftsjthsd-h** 认为漏洞仅在本地可被利用，且需要手动启用可选功能，这比预期的要好，降低了其严重性。

• **amiga386** 引用了 CVE 记录，质疑漏洞类型是否会被更新为更准确的 CWE 分类，并询问之前关于另一个漏洞的模糊信息具体指的是什么。

• **mvdtnz** 对之前 Rachel 的模糊发帖动机表示疑问，认为没有必要如此模糊，质疑是否存在 NDA 或其他合理原因。

• **stiild** 提出了一个与主讨论无关的问题，询问有哪些易于使用和解析的进程监控工具，适合非专职服务器管理员使用。

• **taspeotis** 以调侃的语气评论了漏洞修复中对字符串解析的改进，暗示了语言特性可能带来的潜在问题。

• **nubinetwork** 认为 atop 的问题是由于它期望与特定程序通信，这种问题在很多程序中都存在。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点之一是漏洞的实际影响，部分人认为漏洞仅在本地可被利用且需要启用特定功能，因此危害不大；但其他人则对 atop 使用 TCP 端口的设计选择表示不满，认为这增加了安全隐患。
- 另一个值得注意的点是对之前模糊发帖动机的质疑，部分评论者对信息披露的方式和时机表示困惑。

总体来看，讨论主要围绕漏洞的技术细节、设计缺陷和实际影响展开，部分评论者对漏洞的严重性存在不同看法。

Message-ID: <53411a5a-3b7f-4993-a66e-8e93cd2efb1c@atoptool.nl>
Date: Sat, 29 Mar 2025 18:39:29 +0100
From: Gerlof Langeveld <gerlof.langeveld@...ptool.nl>
To: oss-security@...ts.openwall.com
Subject: CVE-2025-31160 Atop 2.11 heap problems
Introduction:
Atop mainly reads the system level and process level from the /proc and
/sys directories. However, certain counters might be obtained from other
optional sources, that have to be activated explicitly.
One of these sources is the 'atopgpud' daemon, which permanently gathers
metrics about the utilization of GPUs. It offers a local TCP port to which
atop can connect to retrieve GPU-related counters. These counters are
provided as strings that have to be parsed by atop.
Vulnerability:
The vulnerability is caused by the fact that atop always tries to connect
to the TCP port of 'atopgpud' during initialization. When another local
program has been started (instead of 'atopgpud') that listens to this TCP
port, atop connects to that program. Such program is able then to send
unexpected strings that may lead to parsing failures in atop. These failures
result in heap problems and segmentation faults.
Although no additional information has been received about these heap
problems, the described heap problems were reproduced with a custom
developed test program.
The vulnerability is present since the introduction of 'atopgpud'
in atop 2.4.0.
Solution:
1) Most systems will not explicitly activate the 'atopgpud' daemon.
Therefore, the default behavior of atop is now not to connect to the TCP
port at all. Only when atop is started with the '-k' flag it will try to
connect to the TCP port (in case you know that 'atopgpud' is running).
2) When the '-k' flag is used, the parsing of the strings is improved to
avoid that heap problems can occur.
3) Another optional source for atop might be 'netatop' or 'netatop-bpf'.
Since most systems will not explicitly install/use these sources,
the default
behavior of atop is now not to try to find these sources. Only when
atop is
started with the '-K' flag it will try to find 'netatop' or
'netatop-bpf'.

43518560.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Openwall项目中ATOP工具的一个安全漏洞（CVE-2025-31160），该漏洞源于ATOP尝试连接一个未明确激活的'atopgpud'守护进程的TCP端口，可能导致堆问题和段错误。解决方案包括修改默认行为，使ATOP不再自动连接TCP端口，除非使用特定启动标志（-k），并改进字符串解析以避免问题。同时，对于其他可选来源如'netatop'，也需通过特定标志（-K）启用，以防止类似问题。文章还提供了漏洞的背景、影响及修复建议。
43518560.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕软件工具 "atop" 漏洞的发现、影响及设计问题的讨论

不同观点：
• **ianbutler** 认为他们的工具 Bismuth 成功找到了漏洞，并提供了重现脚本的 SHA 作为证明，详细描述了发现过程，并分享了技术报告链接。他确认了漏洞的发现并公开了相关信息。

• **geerlingguy** 指出，这个漏洞并没有之前帖子暗示的那么严重，原本期待的是供应链攻击级别的严重问题，但实际发现的问题相对轻微。

• **cullenking** 分享了自己过去使用 atop 时遇到的类似问题，指出 atop 在设计上可能因为需要挂钩到多个系统位置而产生意外的后果，但他并不认为这是开发者的错。

• **unsnap_biceps** 和 **Zardoz84** 都对 atop 使用 TCP 端口而不是 Unix socket 进行本地连接表示不满，认为这是一种不良设计，可能导致不必要的安全隐患。

• **Galanwe** 质疑漏洞的实际影响，认为如果需要本地权限才能利用该漏洞，那么其危害性相对较低，因为拥有本地权限的攻击者已经可以通过其他手段进行破坏。

• **yjftsjthsd-h** 认为漏洞仅在本地可被利用，且需要手动启用可选功能，这比预期的要好，降低了其严重性。

• **amiga386** 引用了 CVE 记录，质疑漏洞类型是否会被更新为更准确的 CWE 分类，并询问之前关于另一个漏洞的模糊信息具体指的是什么。

• **mvdtnz** 对之前 Rachel 的模糊发帖动机表示疑问，认为没有必要如此模糊，质疑是否存在 NDA 或其他合理原因。

• **stiild** 提出了一个与主讨论无关的问题，询问有哪些易于使用和解析的进程监控工具，适合非专职服务器管理员使用。

• **taspeotis** 以调侃的语气评论了漏洞修复中对字符串解析的改进，暗示了语言特性可能带来的潜在问题。

• **nubinetwork** 认为 atop 的问题是由于它期望与特定程序通信，这种问题在很多程序中都存在。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点之一是漏洞的实际影响，部分人认为漏洞仅在本地可被利用且需要启用特定功能，因此危害不大；但其他人则对 atop 使用 TCP 端口的设计选择表示不满，认为这增加了安全隐患。
- 另一个值得注意的点是对之前模糊发帖动机的质疑，部分评论者对信息披露的方式和时机表示困惑。

总体来看，讨论主要围绕漏洞的技术细节、设计缺陷和实际影响展开，部分评论者对漏洞的严重性存在不同看法。

data.title: It’s not mold, it’s calcium lactate (2018)
data.author: ilikepi
data.article_summary: 本文主要讨论了奶酪中出现的晶体，尤其是陈年奶酪中常见的钙乳酸盐晶体。作者解释说，这些晶体常常被误认为是霉菌，但实际上是无味无嗅的，且对奶酪的风味没有直接影响。文章区分了两类晶体："无机晶体"和"有机晶体"。无机晶体由矿物质形成，如磷酸钙、Ikaite和Struvite，而有机晶体则由蛋白质分解过程中产生的氨基酸形成，如酪氨酸晶体和亮氨酸晶体。钙乳酸盐晶体通常出现在无外皮的陈年切达奶酪上，是奶酪熟成良好的标志。这些晶体提供了不同的感官体验，如咬合时的脆感或粗糙感，是奶酪爱好者寻找的风味标志。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：

• [WillPostForFood] 表达了对含有晶体的优质高达奶酪的喜爱，并提到对晶体（酪氨酸）科学细节的兴趣。
• [geetee] 质疑奶酪制造商可能会人为添加晶体以伪装高质量，而不注重实际质量。

• [dekhn] 讨论了奶酪晶体的鲜味特性，尤其是谷氨酸晶体，并好奇其他氨基酸晶体是否也有类似风味。
• [karaterobot] 提供了关于不同类型奶酪晶体（如乳酸钙、酪氨酸、亮氨酸晶体）形成位置的科学信息。

• [niemandhier] 推荐了一本关于奶酪科学的书《The Science of Cheese》，认为这本书深入且充满热情。

• [talkingtab] 提出市面上很多所谓的“奶酪”并不是传统意义上的奶酪，并分享了自己制作奶酪的经验，包括温度和湿度控制等技术细节。
• [xattt] 提到在碎奶酪包装中发现抗真菌剂纳他霉素，并表达了对长期低水平摄入这种化学物质的潜在健康影响的担忧。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及了奶酪晶体的科学原理（如晶体的种类和形成位置）、奶酪的保存方法（如温度和湿度控制）、以及对市售奶酪质量和添加剂的质疑。
• 争议焦点在于奶酪晶体的自然形成与人为添加以提升外观质量的做法之间的潜在冲突，以及对食品添加剂（如纳他霉素）长期影响的担忧。

43535688.article_content:
Two weeks ago, one of my best friends and ex-cheese comrades, Chelsea, brought our old mentor/boss-lady, the illustrious Kim Martin, into the shop. Neither of them had visited us before, and it was pretty exciting to show them around our little corner of the co-op.
As they were getting ready to leave, Chelsea pulled me aside and silently pointed at a quarter-wheel of aged Gouda on display in the back of the case, tapping the side of it to show me that it was all white.
“It’s not mold,” I announced without skipping a beat. “It’s calcium lactate.”
This is something I actually have to write on the scale label when we wrap wedges of the cheese for sale, because people are inherently put off by a sheet of white on an otherwise butterscotch-orange cheese.
After all, most people are familiar with white, wispy molds growing on the outside of cheese—either as the well-manicured coif of a bloomy-rind cheese or as errant growths on the cut face of half-eaten cheese hunks living in the refrigerator cheese drawer.
But there are other white things that can grow on your cheese, and they are actually desirable: crystals!
You know what I’m referring to if you have bitten into an aged Gouda, Cheddar, or Parmesan and felt that satisfying crunch. You also know it if you’ve sunk your teeth through the sticky orange exterior of a washed-rind cheese and felt a slight grittiness.
People often come into the shop looking for cheeses that have “salt crystals” in them. As you will learn below, there are two “families” of crystals that form in cheese. Only one of those families has anything to do with salt—and those are not usually the ones people go hunting for in a cheese shop. While a cheese might taste salty and have crystals in it, that doesn’t mean the crunchy bits are salt, per se.
The crystals that people really want when they are asking for “salt crystals” are often referred to in the industry as “flavor crystals.” That’s because the sight of these crystals is a sign that you’ve found a flavorful, or fully-developed, cheese.
In fact, cheese crystals don’t have any effect on the way a cheese tastes—they are flavorless and scentless. But they do affect other sensory perceptions of a bite of cheese: sound (crunching), touch (bumpiness or rough texture), and sight (white spots, clusters, or patches).
There are several different types of crystals that grow in or on cheese at different times in the cheese-making or -aging process. They are either going to be the product of mineral (salt) emulsion during cheesemaking or protein breakdown (proteolysis) as the cheese ages.
The crystals you may not notice as much are the “inorganic crystals,” or crystals formed by minerals.
[i]
This “family” of crystals is created when salts emulsify, or disperse throughout the cheese without dissolving, during the cheese-making process.
[ii]
(These are the ones you could call salt crystals.)
For example, calcium phosphate crystals are most commonly found under the rinds of bloomy-rind cheeses, helping them become soft as they ripen.
[iii]
Two other kinds of inorganic crystals, Ikaite and Struvite, are what you notice when a washed-rind cheese has a gritty rind; Ikaite crystals are formed from calcium carbonate, whereas Struvite crystals come from magnesium ammonium phosphate.
[iv]
The crystals that are most noticeable in cheese are the “organic crystals” that are formed by the breakdown of amino acids during the cheese-aging process.
As a cheese ages, it loses moisture and its protein structure contracts and stretches. As this happens, the amino acid chains running through the cheese that make up that protein structure start to break up; the whole process of protein breakdown is called proteolysis.
Each type of organic crystal that you will find in a cheese is named after the amino-acid chain that broke up to create it.
For example, tyrosine crystals give aged goudas their famous crunchy texture. They can grow inside the paste of cheese, or all around the little holes inside a cheese.
Leucine crystals have a similar effect, but have a more diffused, smear-like appearance than tyrosine crystals. Both of these types of crystals may be found in goudas, Alpine-style (Swiss) cheeses, and Grana-style cheeses (e.g., Parmigiano Reggiano, Grana Padano, Piave, etc.).
And then there is calcium lactate, which frequently forms on the outside of rindless cheddars as they age. Calcium lactate formations are seen as a sign that the cheese has aged for a long time and should have a more developed flavor profile.
Calcium lactate originates from an earlier stage of proteolysis, when lactose is still present in the liquid milk that will be fermented into cheese. As the bacterial culture in the cheese eats up all of the lactose, or milk sugar, in the milk, the bacteria create lactic acid.
[v]
Calcium lactate is a byproduct of that lactic acid interacting with calcium carbonate in the cheese over time.
Just in case you were wondering what calcium lactate has to do with amin

data.title: AI Agents: Less Capability, More Reliability, Please
data.author: serjester
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是一个博客订阅邀请和反馈请求。作者邀请读者通过邮件订阅博客以获取最新内容，并鼓励读者提供反馈或提问以增进互动。文章提供了订阅链接和联系方式，旨在建立与读者的长期联系并获取意见。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI代理工具的现状、可靠性、适用场景及局限性

不同观点：
• **Simonw**：认为文章低估了让AI代理完成单一任务的难度。他指出，人类语言输入存在无限变体，无法针对所有可能的情况进行测试，且人类不善于准确表达需求，这使得任务执行容易出错。
• **Wiradikusuma**：表示连人类助理都难以完成他的航班预订任务，因为涉及复杂的比价和决策过程，AI更难以胜任。
• **Danso**：引用了Reddit上的讨论，表达了对依赖AI编程的新工程师缺乏基础编程知识的担忧，但也认为这为自己这样的传统工程师提供了职业安全感。
• **Joshdavham**：强调在使用AI生成代码时，必须能够理解代码，不能像一些“凭感觉编程”的开发者那样依赖AI生成自己不理解的代码。
• **Piokoch**：批评了Cursor项目缺乏版本控制的功能，认为像Aider这样的免费工具在版本控制方面做得更好。
• **Narmiouh**：认为不应责怪AI工具在版本控制问题上的表现，因为这是用户技能不足所致，且有一些SAAS应用更适合这些新手用户。
• **Andreash**：提到正在开发更具确定性的代理，并推荐阅读关于代理定义的文章，暗示未来对代理的需求会增加。
• **Bhu8**：支持工作流自动化优于代理自动化，认为当前代理不可靠，工作流自动化可以提供更高的精度和可诊断性。
• **Ankit219**：指出代理在低信任环境中有用，但在高信任环境中的错误成本太高，代理的错误可能会导致严重后果。
• **Twotwotwo**：基于自己的经验，认为可靠性比速度更重要，AI工具在成熟代码库中的表现不如预期，需要更多的前期工作来减少问题。
• **SkyPuncher**：认为Cursor的例子不恰当，因为其主要用户群是初级程序员，他们面临的问题不完全代表工具本身的问题。同时指出，许多AI助手在广告中宣称的功能在实际使用中无法实现。
• **Hirako2000**：批评AI代理的“黑盒”性质和不可靠性，认为 stochastic machines 不具备真正的智能和推理能力，对相关文章回避这一核心问题感到厌烦。
• **_cs2017_**：对AI代理的实际应用场景持怀疑态度，认为现有AI工具如代码助手已经很好，但在其他如邮件和旅行预订等高成本任务中不可信任。
• **Dfxm12**：认为Google Flights等传统工具在用户体验上已经做得很好，AI代理在可靠性上还无法与之相比。
• **Shireboy**：强调用户缺乏版本控制知识是问题的核心，认为AI工具应该帮助用户设置版本控制以避免问题。

补充讨论：
• **AI工具的可靠性和适用性**：讨论中多次提到AI工具在实际应用中的不可靠性和错误成本，特别是在高信任环境中的应用。
• **用户技能和工具的关系**：强调用户的基础知识和技能对AI工具使用效果的影响，如版本控制和代码理解能力。
• **未来发展方向**：一些讨论者提到工作流自动化可能优于代理自动化，并提到未来对更具确定性代理的需求。
• **现有工具的比较**：一些讨论者将AI工具与传统工具进行比较，认为传统工具在某些任务上更可靠。

争议焦点：
• **AI工具的可靠性和适用场景**：一部分人认为AI工具在某些任务上不可靠，另一部分人则认为这只是用户技能不足所致。
• **代理 vs 工作流**：讨论中存在对代理和工作流自动化哪一个更优的争论。

data.title: Things I Won't Work With: Dioxygen Difluoride (2010)
data.author: PebblesRox
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕含氟化合物（尤其是二氧化二氟，又称FOOF）的特性和应用的讨论

不同观点：
• ChrisMarshallNY和wiredfool欣赏文中对化学反应的生动描述，认为这种写作风格引人入胜，特别是描述氟在高温下解离成单原子自由基的过程，尽管反应产物更糟糕。
• stuartjohnson12质疑杭州市赛智化工有限公司提供的二氧化二氟产品，认为该公司不可能提供这种物质，并讽刺性地建议索要免费 shipping。
• IlikeKitties将二氧化二氟与氯三氟化物的危险性相比较，引用了Gizmodo文章中提到的氯三氟化物能点燃接触到的各种物质，包括玻璃、砂子、石棉、混凝土等。
• perihelions提供了与二氧化二氟及类似危险化学品相关的历史讨论链接，扩展了讨论背景。
• GarnetFloride提到Rocketdyne三推进剂火箭中使用了产生FOOF的化合物，尽管提高了比冲，但由于副产物包括氢氟酸，未能广泛应用。
• rbanffy对从未接触过这种分子感到庆幸，认为文章读起来令人愉快。
• tonetegeatinst表示通过研究发现可以获得氟气，并能压缩在罐中，提供了实际操作的可能性。
• relwin提供了YouTube上关于氟实验室的视频链接，丰富了讨论内容。
• ourmandave以幽默方式指出“二氧化二氟”两个词都以“DIe”开头，暗示其危险性。
• bovermyer开玩笑地问是否还能从中国供应商处订购“撒旦的泡菜”（即二氧化二氟）。
• pazimzadeh担心此讨论与近期自来水中氟化物争议有关，暗示可能引发公众对化学物质的过度担忧。
• api提到一本书《Ignition》中讨论了使用氟作为氧化剂的实验，尽管能提高比冲，但排气是高温下的氢氟酸，存在危险。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中的一个焦点是二氧化二氟的实际存在性和可获得性，特别是stuartjohnson12和bovermyer对此表示怀疑和调侃。
• 另一个值得注意的点是化学物质的危险性和实际应用，IlikeKitties和api提到的氯三氟化物和氟作为氧化剂的实验都强调了这一点。
• 整体讨论气氛较为轻松幽默，但涉及的化学知识和技术问题具有严肃性和专业性。

data.title: Symmetry between up and down quarks is more broken than expected
data.author: terminalbraid
data.article_summary: 2023年底，Wojciech Brylinski在分析CERN的NA61/SHINE合作项目的数据时发现，氩-钪碰撞中带电K介子比中性K介子多产生18.4%，这一异常现象打破了预期的上夸克和下夸克间的同位旋对称性。现有理论模型难以解释这种偏差，因为已知的同位旋不对称性仅预测百分之几的偏差。该结果显示，电磁相互作用可能在产生夸克-反夸克对中起到重要作用，或者强相互作用并不遵循味对称性，这与量子色动力学（QCD）的当前理解相矛盾。研究团队计划进一步研究这一现象，并呼吁理论物理学家帮助解释这一 unexpected 的大不对称性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对对称破缺的影响和理解

不同观点：
• [Just gluon]: 该评论以幽默的方式建议通过"粘合"对称破缺来解决问题，暗示不需要过多关注对称破缺的影响，可能认为当前问题并不严重。

• [ptsneves]: 关注对称破缺的后果，提出当前模型不易解释这种不对称，并询问如果这些模型是错误的，我们的理解会受到哪些影响。该评论关注模型错误可能带来的广泛影响，表明对科学理解的潜在风险的关切。

• [bananapub]: 建议直接链接到CERN的官方新闻稿，可能认为讨论中的信息来源不够权威或准确，强调应依赖官方发布的信息。

• [ars]: 对isospin（同位旋）的定义和使用提出质疑，认为isospin只是描述上夸克和下夸克数量的比率，而非如自旋或电荷般是基本性质。该评论对术语的过时性提出批评，指出其在描述更多种类夸克时的局限性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对科学术语精确性的关注（如isospin的定义和使用），以及对信息来源可靠性的重视（建议参考CERN的官方发布）。
• 存在对理论模型在解释新现象时可能失效的担忧，特别是这些模型失效对当前物理理解的潜在影响。
• 争议焦点在于如何理解和处理对称破缺的影响，以及在讨论中应使用哪些信息来源和术语。

Symmetry between up and down quarks is more broken than expected
by Alex Epshtein,
CERN
NA61/SHINE’s lead-scintillator calorimeter. Credit: CERN
In late 2023, Wojciech Brylinski was analyzing data from the NA61/SHINE collaboration at CERN for his thesis when he noticed an unexpected anomaly—a strikingly large imbalance between charged and neutral kaons in argon–scandium collisions. He found that, instead of being produced in roughly equal numbers, charged kaons were produced 18.4% more often than neutral kaons.
This suggested that the so-called "isospin
symmetry
" between up and down quarks might be broken by more than expected due to the differences in their electric charges and masses—a discrepancy that existing
theoretical models
would struggle to explain. Known sources of isospin asymmetry only predict deviations of a few percent.
"When Wojciech got started, we thought it would be a trivial verification of the symmetry," says Marek Gaździcki, who was spokesperson of NA61/SHINE at the time of the discovery. "We expected the symmetry to be closely obeyed—although we had previously measured these types of discrepancies at the NA49 experiment, they had large uncertainties and were not significant."
Isospin symmetry is one facet of flavor symmetry, whereby the
strong interaction
treats all quark flavors identically. This means that all types of quarks should behave the same under the strong interaction, except for kinematic differences arising from their different masses. Isospin is not a symmetry of the electromagnetic interaction as up and down quarks have different electric charges.
According to isospin symmetry, strong interactions in heavy-ion collisions should generate nearly equal amounts of charged kaons (comprising either an up quark and a strange antiquark or an up antiquark and a strange quark) and neutral kaons (comprising either a down quark and a strange antiquark or a down antiquark and a strange quark), given the similar masses of the up and down quarks. NA61/SHINE's
data contradicts the hypothesis
of equal yields with a 4.7σ significance.
"I see two ways to interpret the results," says Francesco Giacosa, a theoretical physicist working with NA61/SHINE. "First, we might be substantially underestimating the role of electromagnetic interactions in creating
quark
–antiquark pairs. Second, these results could mean that strong interactions do not obey flavor symmetry. If this is true, it would contradict physicists' current understanding of
quantum chromodynamics
(QCD), that is, how quarks and gluons (carriers of the strong interaction) combine."
While the experiment routinely measures particle yields in nuclear collisions, finding a discrepancy in isospin symmetry was not something the researchers were actively looking for. NA61/SHINE's primary focus is studying the properties of the production of hadrons when beams from CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron collide with a variety of fixed nuclear targets. This data is also shared with neutrino and cosmic ray experiments, such as T2K, to help them to refine their models.
The collaboration is now planning additional studies on this new result, using different projectiles, targets and collision energies to determine whether this effect is unique to certain heavy-ion collisions or is a more general feature of high-energy interactions. It has also put out a call to theoretical physicists to help explain what might have caused such an unexpectedly large asymmetry.
"We tried to fit the data into the current, existing models, but it didn't work at all—it was just not possible," says Giacosa. "We need more
experimental data
and more theoretical predictions to fill our gap in knowledge of the strong interaction. So the real question is: what's next?"

data.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro vs. Claude 3.7 Sonnet: Coding Comparison
data.author: mraniki
data.article_summary: Google最新发布的Gemini 2.5 Pro模型在编码、推理等各方面表现优异，尤其在编码方面超越了此前表现最佳的Claude 3.7 Sonnet模型。文章通过四个编码测试（飞行模拟器、Rubik’s Cube解算器等）对比了这两个模型，结果显示Gemini 2.5 Pro在功能实现和准确性上均优于Claude 3.7 Sonnet。Gemini 2.5 Pro拥有100万token的上下文窗口（未来将扩展至200万），并且可以免费使用，使其在综合表现上更具优势。尽管Claude 3.7 Sonnet表现也不差，但相比之下，Gemini 2.5 Pro是当前更好的选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）在编程任务中的能力和局限，以及不同模型的对比和应用场景。

不同观点：
• **phkahler** 认为当前的LLM（包括GPT等）无法胜任将Solvespace从GTK3移植到GTK4的任务，并表示如果有人能用AI完成这个任务，他愿意设置奖金。他怀疑AI能否在实际编程任务中表现出色。
• **qwertox** 认为Gemini在上下文长度和决策方面表现优异，尤其是在处理长时间对话时比ChatGPT表现更好，但工具支持不如ChatGPT。他相信Gemini的核心能力更强，但目前工具链上仍有不足。
• **HarHarVeryFunny** 对AI能否处理10K行代码级别的复杂项目表示怀疑，认为AI目前只在处理局部任务和简单任务时有用，且需要用户的大量指导。他期待未来模型的改进。
• **neal_** 认为Gemini在某些方面表现不错，但总体上改进有限，且一些免费模型（如deepseek）表现优于付费模型。他对当前大公司模型的市场价值表示怀疑。
• **bratao** 对Gemini的编码能力持否定态度，尤其是在处理复杂代码时，Gemini经常做出不相关的修改，导致代码损坏。他认为Claude在处理他的项目时表现更好。
• **antirez** 认为Gemini在复杂代码的推理和审查方面有优势，尽管在通用任务上不如Claude，但在特定场景下表现更好。
• **kingkongjaffa** 认为原讨论中对Gemini的评价过于偏颇，且有广告嫌疑，对Gemini的流行和性能提出质疑。

43534029.article_content:
Google just launched Gemini 2.5 Pro on March 26th, claiming to be the best in coding, reasoning and overall everything. But I mostly care about how the model compares against the best available coding model, Claude 3.7 Sonnet (thinking), released at the end of February, which I have been using, and it has been a great experience.
Let’s compare these two coding models and see if I need to change my favourite coding model or if Claude 3.7 still holds.
TL;DR
If you want to jump straight to the conclusion, I’d say go for
Gemini 2.5 Pro
, it’s better at coding, has one million in context window as compared to Claude’s 200k, and you can get it for free (a big plus). However, Claude’s 3.7 Sonnet is not that far behind. Though at this point there’s no point using it over Gemini 2.5 Pro.
Just an article ago,
Claude 3.7 Sonnet
was the default answer to every model comparison, and this remained the same for quite some time. But here you go, Gemini 2.5 Pro takes the lead.
Brief on Gemini 2.5 Pro
Gemini 2.5 Pro, an experimental thinking model, became the talk of the town within a week of its release. Everyone’s talking about this model on Twitter (X) and YouTube. It’s trending everywhere, like seriously. The first model from Google to receive such fanfare.
And it is
#1 in the LMArena
just like that. But what does this mean? It means that this model is killing all the other models in coding, math, Science, Image understanding, and other areas.
Gemini 2.5 pro comes with a
1 million token context window,
with a 2 million context window coming soon. 🤯
You can check out other folks like
Theo-t3
talking about this model to get a bit more insight into it:
It is the best coding model to date, with an accuracy of about 63.8% on the SWE bench. This is definitely higher than our previous top coding model, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, which had an accuracy of about 62.3%.
This is a quick demo Google shared on this model of building a dinosaur game.
Here’s a quick benchmark of this model on Reasoning, Mathematics, and Science. This confirms that the model is not just suitable for coding but also for all your other needs. They claim it’s an all-rounder. 🤷‍♂️
This is all cool, and I’ll confirm the claim, but in this article, I will mainly be comparing the model on coding, and let’s see how well it performs compared to Claude 3.7 Sonnet.
Coding Problems
Let’s compare these two models in coding. We’ll do a total of 4 tests, mainly on WebDev, animation and a tricky LeetCode question.
1. Flight Simulator
Prompt:
Create a simple flight simulator using JavaScript. The simulator should feature a basic plane that can take off from a flat runway. The plane’s movement should be controlled with simple keyboard inputs (e.g., arrow keys or WASD). Additionally, it generates a basic cityscape using blocky structures, similar to Minecraft.
Response from Gemini 2.5 Pro
You can find the code it generated here:
Link
Here’s the output of the program:
I definitely got exactly what I asked for, with everything functioning, from plane movements to the basic Minecraft-styled block buildings. I can’t really complain about anything here. 10/10 for this one.
Response from Claude 3.7 Sonnet
You can find the code it generated here:
Link
Here’s the output of the program:
I can see some issues with this one. The plane clearly faces sideways, and I don’t know why. Again, it was out of control once it took off and went clearly outside the city. Basically, I’d say we didn’t really get a completely working flight simulator here.
Summary:
It’s fair to say that Gemini 2.5 really got this correct in one shot. But the issues with the Claude 3.7 Sonnet code aren’t really that big to resolve. Yeah, we didn’t really get the output as expected, and it’s definitely not close to what Gemini 2.5 Pro got us.
2. Rubik’s Cube Solver
This is one of the toughest questions for LLMs. I’ve tried it with many other LLMs, but none could correct it. Let’s see how these two models do this one.
Prompt:
Build a simple 3D Rubik’s Cube visualizer and solver in JavaScript using Three.js. The cube should be a 3×3 Rubik’s Cube with standard colours. Have a scramble button that randomly scrambles the cube. Include a solve function that animates the solution step by step. Allow basic mouse controls to rotate the view.
Response from Gemini 2.5 Pro
You can find the code it generated here:
Link
Here’s the output of the program:
It’s impressive that it could do something this hard in one shot. With the 1 million token context window, I can truly see how powerful this model seems to be.
Response from Claude 3.7 Sonnet
You can find the code it generated here:
Link
Here’s the output of the program:
Again, I was kind of disappointed that it had the same issue as some other LLMs: failing with the colours and completely failing to solve the cube. I did try to help it come up with the answer, but it didn’t really help.
Summary:
Here again, Gemini 2.5 Pro takes the lead. And the best part is that all of it was done in one

data.title: The <select> element can now be customized with CSS
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: Chrome 135引入了可自定义的`<select>`元素，支持CSS样式，使开发者可以创建更具可访问性和标准化的下拉菜单。新的`appearance: base-select` CSS属性允许对`<select>`内部结构和行为进行深度定制，包括支持在选项中使用HTML内容（如图片和SVG）。虽然这些变化提供了更高的灵活性，但也带来了潜在的兼容性风险，Chrome通过Finch实验控制该功能。JavaScript接口保持不变，但如果在选项中添加复杂HTML，需注意选定值的处理。目前Chrome率先实现该功能，未来将有更多浏览器跟进。详细信息和示例可参阅文末资源链接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Chrome浏览器中可自定义的 <select> 元素及其相关功能和影响

不同观点：
• [wolframhempel] 对新功能的热情，认为新功能（如下拉选项可超出视口边界）非常有帮助，并期待自动完成和标签选择器的类似改进。
• [ljoshua] 关注新功能的浏览器兼容性（目前全球支持率为46%），强调渐进增强的必要性，确保不支持新功能的浏览器用户不会遇到使用问题，同时引用了caniuse.com的数据作为论据。
• [nasso_dev] 担心新功能可能取代内置的移动操作系统组件，认为内置组件更可靠、易访问且响应迅速，尤其对Android用户而言。
• [Brysonbw] 期待此功能能推动更多原生Web功能的实现，减少开发者对第三方库的依赖。
• [butz] 认为有些控件不应自定义样式，举例说明自定义滚动条可能导致用户体验问题，强调默认选择控件虽不美观但功能可靠。

补充讨论：
• [dpcx] 认为这是开发者期待数十年的功能，可能最终替代JS库的功能，但对多选字段的处理方式存在疑问。
• [chias] 指出<select>元素目前仅能在Chromium浏览器中通过CSS自定义。
• [rsingel] 以讽刺口吻指出Chrome开发博客未能通过Google自身的Core Web Vitals测试，质疑新功能的实际效果。
• [klabb3] 对新功能持谨慎态度，关注选项过多时的布局和用户交互问题，同时对Floating UI的实验性特性表示兴趣。
• [johnthuss] 对新功能表示欢迎，希望Safari浏览器能快速采纳此功能。
• [ichik] 报告在Firefox 136.0.2中新功能存在显示问题，如下拉菜单缺失背景/框。
• [wg0] 回顾了自2009年以来对Web技术构建UI的信心增强，认为Web技术是最开放和跨平台的。
• [hk1337] 对新功能的美观性表示认可，但认为大多数情况下基本样式已足够，并批评Chrome正逐渐变成它曾反对的（如IE）。
• [Onavo] 询问是否能实现完全原生的组合框（comobobox）。

争议焦点：
• 新功能的美观性与实用性之间的平衡。
• 自定义选择控件与内置操作系统组件的可靠性和用户体验比较。
• 新功能的浏览器兼容性和渐进增强策略。
• 自定义样式可能导致的用户体验问题，如滚动条设计。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 对多选字段处理和布局问题的技术细节探讨。
• 新功能在不同浏览器中的实现情况和存在的问题。
• 对Chrome自身Core Web Vitals测试失败的批评。
• 对Web技术演进和跨平台优势的长期信心。

43532830.article_content: Chrome for Developers Blog The element on the web. This has been many years in the making, many hours of engineering and collaborative specification work, and the result is an incredibly rich and powerful component that won't break in older browsers. Here's a video of customized selects using these new features: Featuring demos by Una , Brecht , and Adam . If you've been following along closely, you'll notice a few spec names and features have changed since Una 's request for community feedback . Luckily, if you worked from that post and are interested in what's changed, Una's also got you covered . There's also shiny new documentation on MDN for customizable select , packed with details. Meet appearance: base-select A new CSS property appearance: base-select that puts the . Changes the rendered internals of the . A new minimal look, optimized for customization. Shown options are in the top-layer, like a popover. Shown options positioned with anchor() . Using base-select loses a number of features and behaviors: The stops taking the width of the longest Here's (from left to right) Chrome, Safari, and Firefox rendering the preceding HTML. If the browser supports appearance: base-select then the SVG will appear in the option, otherwise it won't. Try it in this Codepen . There's risk in breaking existing websites with customizable select, due to the parser changes. Chrome has the features behind a Finch experiment in case there is an emergency need to turn it off. If things go well, the experiment will end and the code will be shipped permanently into the source. Completely customizable Every part of a base-select can be swapped out, customized and animated. Here's a demo that uses every new feature to create recognizable and meaningful select experiences. Try it in this Codepen . Find many more examples in the resources section at the end of this post. data.title: Unmasking a slow and steady password spray attack
data.author: noleary
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Password Spraying攻击的有效性、检测方法及安全性措施

不同观点：
• [barbazoo] 认为Password Spraying是一种暴力攻击，攻击者会使用默认密码对多个账户进行尝试，以避免因对单个账户使用多个密码而被锁定。这种攻击常见于新用户被设置默认密码的场景。

• [jsnell] 对这种攻击的有效性表示怀疑，认为Password Spraying的产出率很低，需要高数量的尝试来弥补。例如，每周24次尝试不足以构成有效攻击。

• [Liftyee] 从一个非网络安全背景的角度出发，认为在每个账户只能尝试2次的情况下，攻击者仍尝试这些攻击令人惊讶。除非大量使用常见密码，否则成功概率极低。然而，由于攻击的潜在回报高且执行成本接近于零，这种攻击仍然值得尝试。

• [giorgioz] 对如何将24个用户在一周内被攻击的情况识别为恶意攻击感到困惑，并对文章中提到的使用/48前缀来逃避检测表示不解。同时，认为仅查看用户活动时间线不足以检测基础设施攻击。

• [grayhatter] 指出IPv6地址在低于/64的粒度上没有意义，并认为使用ASN比根据国家来源进行过滤更有效。对文章中仅通过查看用户活动时间线来检测攻击的方法表示不信任，认为内容过于表面。

• [yellow_lead] 建议启用双因素身份验证（2FA）以增强安全性，而不是仅仅依赖密码。
