data.title: Bluesky isn't just another Twitter/X competitor. It fixes social media
data.author: herbertl
data.article_summary: Bluesky是一个不同于Twitter/X的社交媒体平台，解决了现有社交媒体的诸多问题。自2023年夏季以来，由于埃隆·马斯克对Twitter/X的收购及其后续改革，大量用户逃离至Bluesky，使其用户数迅速增长，目前已达3380万。与Twitter和Meta的Threads不同，Bluesky基于开放源代码的AT Protocol，用户拥有自己的社交身份和数据，可以自由迁移至其他平台而无需承担启动成本。这种设计使得Bluesky在用户体验和平台开放性方面独具优势，吸引了包括奥巴马在内的众多知名用户和媒体机构。Bluesky的开放性可能改变社交网络的未来发展方向，使用户不再被锁定于单一平台。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社交媒体（尤其是Bluesky）的优缺点及其未来发展

不同观点：
• [mnky9800n] 认为社交媒体的问题在于信息获取和反应的速度过快，这让人没有时间去思考和消化信息。他担心大量随机信息没有实际价值，对大脑有害。

• [jauntywundrkind] 支持Bluesky，认为它赋予用户持续塑造和改进社交媒体的能力，避免了单一决策者的控制。他强调Bluesky提供的开放性和可能性，并提到Bluesky与其他社交媒体（如ActivityPub）的不同，后者需要多账户来实现不同功能。

• [4ndrewl] 持怀疑态度，认为即使Bluesky目前有优势，但一旦被大公司收购，可能会失去其独特性或优点。

• [1970-01-01] 认为Bluesky只解决了一个社交媒体的问题，但还有其他重要问题未解决，如内容审核和对抗权威政府的审查。他提到AI审核和人类审核的潜在问题，并引用马斯克收购Twitter的例子，警示未来可能面临的威胁。

• [wolvesechoes] 持反对意见，认为Bluesky没有解决社交媒体的根本问题，反而延续了这些问题，暗示社交媒体本质上就是问题所在。

• Bluesky的开放性和分支路径被[jauntywundrkind]视为其主要优势，但其他评论者如[4ndrewl]和[1970-01-01]则关注其未来可能面临的商业收购和审核问题。
• 对Bluesky的未来持怀疑和保留态度的观点主要集中在商业收购和内容审核的潜在风险上。
• 讨论中还涉及了对社交媒体本质问题的反思，如[mnky9800n]和[wolvesechoes]提到的信息过载和缺乏思考时间的问题。

43537854.article_content:
March 31, 2025, 10:34 a.m.
Bluesky isn't just another Twitter/X competitor. It fixes what's wrong with social media.
Crazy Stupid Tech
By Fred Vogelstein
I joined Bluesky as soon as I could get my hands on an invite back in the summer of 2023.  Twitter/X had become an increasingly unpleasant place since Elon Musk bought it in 2022. And then I discovered what many did back then: There weren’t enough users. I stopped using it.
This is the biggest problem for any new social network: It needs to reach a certain size for it to be useful. The trick is getting to that certain size. You have to offer something truly new or be the beneficiary of some galvanizing force to get over that hump. Many thought the changes Musk made to Twitter/X during the first year he owned it would be enough. They weren’t.
Then Donald Trump became President. He made Musk, who’d spent more than any single person in history to help elect him, a top advisor. And that proved to be the final straw. Millions fled Twitter/X all at once to Bluesky. Its user base immediately doubled to 20 million. By the end of January it had hit 30 million. By the time you read this it will be 33.8 million. Bluesky looks like it’s adding
more than 1 million users a month
, based on some of the apps that track that data.
It’s still a fraction of the users on other more established networks. But it’s large enough to be relevant and more importantly, to experience network effect liftoff. That’s where users start joining because it seems like everyone else is joining.
Former President Barack Obama
joined
last week.  Those with
top follower accounts
now include The New York Times, NPR, the Washington Post, investor Mark Cuban, congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, actor George Takei, Rachel Maddow at MSNBC and author Stephen King.  Bluesky’s CEO
Jay Graber’
s
hour-long interview
with board member and journalist
Mike Masnick
was one of the most covered events of the SXSW conference in early March.
It’s tempting to respond to all this with a shrug. Many thought Twitter was a social media cesspool before Musk bought it. Is it progress that we now have two Twitters? Musk turned Twitter/X into the Fox News of social networks. Bluesky - for the moment, anyway - feels like the MSNBC of social networks. So what.
Many of us thought Meta’s Threads might become the next Twitter when it launched in 2023. It certainly got big fast - it now has more than 300 million users - because Meta leveraged its giant Instagram user base. But it’s not much of a news source because of the way Meta manages the algorithm. And of all the social networks I use, it generates the least real engagement. I don’t know why.
But I’m not alone
.
But Bluesky is different because of the way it’s designed. And that’s actually worth attention. It may look like a Twitter/X or Threads competitor. But it’s actually an entirely different thing. Bluesky is built on an open source programming standard called AT Protocol. That makes it the first open source social network to achieve meaningful scale. Many thought Mastodon, built on the similar but older Activity Pub open source protocol would be that. But its growth has flatlined, probably because Bluesky is easier to use. Bluesky feels like using Twitter 15 years ago.
Why is that important? Because users are not locked in.  This isn’t how social networking works today, as we all know.  Social network companies don’t want us to leave. So they’ve made it almost impossible for us to import our social history and network connections into competitors. Everything we do on Bluesky is portable.
What this means is that if someone creates a better version of Bluesky a year from now, we can take our social graph and social history and begin using that new application with zero startup costs. Our social graph and history would travel with us. And we’d still have access to the giant user base Bluesky helped build.
When you create a Bluesky identity, Bluesky actually doesn’t own it, You do. It doesn’t own your network or your social interactions. You do. It doesn’t even own the 34 million person user base.  I just set up
Flashes
, an app that looks a lot like Instagram, except it seamlessly sinks with my Bluesky feed.
Graber, Bluesky’s CEO, knows about these issues first hand. “When I was building a social network back in 2019, I was building an alternative to Facebook events. It was really hard to get the initial network density to get enough people on this app,” she said in the SXSW interview. “And that's the challenge most social network builders face.  But if you have this shared network you can tap into, you can freely build. And all of a sudden you're tapping into a user base of 32 million users, and all the things they've ever posted, all the connections they've already made. And you can build apps that don't require getting from zero to a few thousand users to get over the barrier of relevance. “
It’s not just users that are joining Bluesky because everyone else is. De

• [jauntywundrkind] 支持Bluesky，认为它赋予用户持续塑造和改进社交媒体的能力，避免了单一决策者的控制。他强调Bluesky提供的开放性和可能性，并提到Bluesky与其他社交媒体（如ActivityPub）的不同，后者需要多账户来实现不同功能。

• [4ndrewl] 持怀疑态度，认为即使Bluesky目前有优势，但一旦被大公司收购，可能会失去其独特性或优点。

• [1970-01-01] 认为Bluesky只解决了一个社交媒体的问题，但还有其他重要问题未解决，如内容审核和对抗权威政府的审查。他提到AI审核和人类审核的潜在问题，并引用马斯克收购Twitter的例子，警示未来可能面临的威胁。

• [southernplaces7] 简短回应，暗示Bluesky目前的优势可能只是暂时的。

• [wolvesechoes] 持反对意见，认为Bluesky没有解决社交媒体的根本问题，反而延续了这些问题，暗示社交媒体本质上就是问题所在。

补充讨论：
• Bluesky的开放性和分支路径被[jauntywundrkind]视为其主要优势，但其他评论者如[4ndrewl]和[1970-01-01]则关注其未来可能面临的商业收购和审核问题。
• 对Bluesky的未来持怀疑和保留态度的观点主要集中在商业收购和内容审核的潜在风险上。
• 讨论中还涉及了对社交媒体本质问题的反思，如[mnky9800n]和[wolvesechoes]提到的信息过载和缺乏思考时间的问题。

• [icy] 介绍了Tangled，一个基于AT Protocol的Git协作平台，重新思考和改进了GitHub的现状，强调了开放源码和持续构建。

• [itwenty] 发布了MergeFit应用，解决了Apple Watch用户在记录运动时误结束活动导致数据分割的问题。
• [greysteil] 构建了mentions.us，提供关键词在多个平台被提及的提醒服务，强调了技术挑战和个人成就感。

data.title: Marine Le Pen barred from running for office for 5 years
data.author: jpcom
data.article_summary: 法国极右翼政治家马琳·勒庞因挪用欧盟资金被判五年内不得竞选公职，并被处以四年监禁，其中两年缓刑。这一判决立即生效，可能使她无法参加2027年的总统选举。勒庞被指控在2004至2016年担任欧洲议会议员期间，将用于议会助理的资金挪用于政党活动。勒庞计划提起上诉，但法国媒体认为上诉过程可能漫长，无法确保在2027年选举前完成。国民联盟主席巴德拉表示，这一判决不公正，称法国民主遭到打击。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

43538512.article_content:
Marine Le Pen barred from running for office for 5 years
French far-right politician Marine Le Pen has been barred from standing for office for five years with immediate effect after being convicted of embezzling EU funds. The ruling is likely to rule her out of the 2027 presidential race.
Le Pen was accused of misappropriating money intended for European Union parliamentary aides to finance her party's activities when she was a member of European Parliament between 2004 and 2016.
A court in Paris on Monday gave her a five-year ban on running for public office and a four-year prison sentence, two years of which are suspended.
The former head of the National Rally party is widely viewed as the frontrunner for the 2027 presidential election. She needs to have Monday's ruling overturned by a higher court in order to revive her chance of running in the election.
Le Pen plans to appeal. But French newspaper Le Monde said, "the fact that such cases are often met with particularly long delays makes it uncertain that an appeals trial could be held before the 2027 presidential election."
National Rally President Jordan Bardella wrote on social media that, " Today it is not only Marine Le Pen who was unjustly condemned: It was French democracy that was killed."

data.title: The average college student today
data.author: Jyaif
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：当代大学教育的质量、目的和面临的挑战

不同观点：
• **大学教育的交易性质**：[jt-hill] 认为大学教育对学生来说主要是交易性的，学生购买的是文凭这个“白领工作许可”，而非真正的学习体验。教授要求更多会被视为浪费学生时间。
• **教育标准和淘汰机制**：[c0redump] 认为虽然应该对不合格的学生进行淘汰，但现实中由于各种压力很难执行，尽管从道德角度看这是正确的做法。
• **技术对教育的负面影响**：[mppm] 指出LLMs（大型语言模型）正在严重影响教育质量，学生依赖AI导致实际技能下降，未来可能产生大量无法就业的“毕业生”。
• **缺勤和学习态度的变化**：[joshdavham] 提到缺勤问题并非新现象，一些学生认为如果课程内容只是照本宣科，那么自学可能更有效率。
• **经济不平等对教育的影响**：[jgord] 强调经济不平等加剧了学生需要打工维持学业，导致他们没有时间广泛阅读或深度思考，而这种不平等也影响了整个社会的创新能力。
• **教育质量的下降**：[silcoon] 分享了其在欧洲大学的经历，指出教授因学生压力而降低教学难度以保住职位，导致教育质量下降。
• **学生能力的变化**：[specialp] 质疑当代学生的“文盲”现象，是否因为他们习惯于简洁直接的表达方式而无法适应复杂的文学作品。
• **技术依赖与教育方式的转变**：[andrewvc] 提到学生对手机和技术的依赖，并建议禁止K-12教育阶段使用手机以提高学习效果。
• **课程内容和评估的简化**：[JimBlackwood] 认为课程内容简化和学生参与度下降是当前教育面临的主要问题，疫情后这一现象更加明显。
• **教育目的的根本变化**：[martindbp] 认为整个教育体系的目的正在崩溃，从学前教育到大学，互联网和AI正在改变学习方式，传统教育在学习、社交、职业培训等方面的价值都在下降。

补充讨论：
• **作弊问题和技术应对**：[airstrike] 提到学生利用AI作弊的现象严重，并提出未来可能的技术解决方案，如个性化文本生成和水印技术以防止作弊。
• **人口变化对教育的影响**：[pacbard] 从统计数据出发，解释大学入学率的提高导致学生平均素质下降，因为更多来自较低百分位的学生进入大学。
• **学生基础能力的下降**：[austin-cheney] 指出精英大学的学生甚至无法完整阅读一本小说，这影响了他们的工作能力和沟通技巧，导致对AI和大型框架的过度依赖。

争议焦点：
• 大学教育是否应该严格淘汰不合格学生，尽管这在政治和社会上可能不可行。
• 技术（如AI）对教育的破坏性影响以及如何有效应对这一挑战。
• 教育目的的根本变化以及传统教育体系如何适应现代社会的需求。

data.author: georgehill
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开放模型的定义、用途和开放程度

不同观点：
• [vessenes] 期望看到一个多模态的开放权重模型，能够作为功能性教师，并提供不同大小的模型以方便训练和微调，同时支持工具调用。
• [syntaxing] 希望有一个性能优于QWQ、具有良好工具调用支持的推理模型，并兼具Qwen2.5的智能和Gemini的个性和创造力。
• [pera] 认为“开放模型”是误用，实际更接近于免费软件或盗版软件，而非真正的开源。
• [bhouston] 质疑开放模型的具体开放程度，包括是否可商用以及训练协议是否公开。
• [kgeist] 希望看到更多语言支持，认为当前的开放权重模型在多语言方面不如GPT3或GPT4。
• [mirzap] 主张OpenAI应将其前沿模型作为开放权重模型发布，认为这样可以确立行业标准并获得长期优势，类似于Google的Android策略。
• [Liwink] 质疑开放源模型的主要用例，特别是在生成NSFW内容方面的使用。
• [turnsout] 认为开放核心技术的举动是出于绝望，并将其商业模式比作SNL中的Change Bank。
• [42lux] 认为开放模型的目的是让企业客户能够在内部部署用于处理“秘密数据”的简单聊天机器人，且模型在一定收入范围内是免费的。
• [CamperBob2] 强调开放模型的使用不应被限定，用户无需解释其具体用途。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于“开放模型”的真正定义及其开放程度，包括是否可商用、训练协议是否公开等。
• 对开放模型的功能需求多样化，包括多模态支持、性能提升、工具调用和多语言支持等。
• 对企业战略的讨论，特别是OpenAI等公司开放其核心技术模型的动机和商业考量。

不同观点：
• [vessenes] 期望看到一个多模态的开放权重模型，能够作为功能性教师，并提供不同大小的模型以方便训练和微调，同时支持工具调用。
• [syntaxing] 希望有一个性能优于QWQ、具有良好工具调用支持的推理模型，并兼具Qwen2.5的智能和Gemini的个性和创造力。
• [pera] 认为“开放模型”是误用，实际更接近于免费软件或盗版软件，而非真正的开源。
• [bhouston] 质疑开放模型的具体开放程度，包括是否可商用以及训练协议是否公开。
• [kgeist] 希望看到更多语言支持，认为当前的开放权重模型在多语言方面不如GPT3或GPT4。
• [mirzap] 主张OpenAI应将其前沿模型作为开放权重模型发布，认为这样可以确立行业标准并获得长期优势，类似于Google的Android策略。
• [Liwink] 质疑开放源模型的主要用例，特别是在生成NSFW内容方面的使用。
• [turnsout] 认为开放核心技术的举动是出于绝望，并将其商业模式比作SNL中的Change Bank。
• [42lux] 认为开放模型的目的是让企业客户能够在内部部署用于处理“秘密数据”的简单聊天机器人，且模型在一定收入范围内是免费的。
• [CamperBob2] 强调开放模型的使用不应被限定，用户无需解释其具体用途。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于“开放模型”的真正定义及其开放程度，包括是否可商用、训练协议是否公开等。
• 对开放模型的功能需求多样化，包括多模态支持、性能提升、工具调用和多语言支持等。
• 对企业战略的讨论，特别是OpenAI等公司开放其核心技术模型的动机和商业考量。

data.title: New blood test checks for Alzheimer's and assesses progression, study
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 研究人员开发了一种血液检测方法，用于检查有思维和记忆问题的人是否患有阿尔茨海默病及其进展程度，从而帮助医生选择最合适的药物。该测试通过检测血液中的tau蛋白碎片（eMTBR-tau243），这些碎片与阿尔茨海默病患者脑中的tau缠结积累相关，但在其他疾病患者中未发现升高。研究涉及902名参与者，结果显示，阿尔茨海默病症状较轻的患者和痴呆患者的tau碎片水平较高，而其他原因导致认知障碍的人则没有升高。尽管该测试科学上很有前景，但仍需进一步验证和简化以普及使用。另一项研究还发现脑脊液中两种蛋白的比例与认知障碍程度相关，有助于预测未来认知衰退和痴呆的发作。

The researchers found fragments of tau could be detected in blood and correlated with a build-up of tau tangles in the brains of people with Alzheimer’s, but not other diseases.
Photograph: Liuhsihsiang/Getty Images
View image in fullscreen
The researchers found fragments of tau could be detected in blood and correlated with a build-up of tau tangles in the brains of people with Alzheimer’s, but not other diseases.
Photograph: Liuhsihsiang/Getty Images
Alzheimer's
New blood test checks for Alzheimer’s and assesses progression, study says
Procedure for patients with thinking and memory problems could help medics decide which drugs are most suitable
Nicola Davis
Science correspondent
Mon 31 Mar 2025 11.00 EDT
Last modified on Mon 31 Mar 2025 11.15 EDT
Share
Researchers have developed a blood test for patients with thinking and memory problems to check if they have Alzheimer’s and to see how far it has progressed.
The team behind the work say the test could help medics decide which drugs would be most suitable for patients. For example, new drugs such as
donanemab
and
lecanemab
can help slow the progression of Alzheimer’s, but only in people in the early stages of the disease.
Prof Oskar Hansson from Lund University, a co-author of the work, said: “There is an urgent need for accurate and cost-effective Alzheimer diagnostics considering that many countries have recently approved the clinical use of amyloid-targeted therapies [such as donanemab and lecanemab].”
Plaques of a protein called amyloid beta and the formation of tangles of another protein called tau in the brain are considered hallmarks of Alzheimer’s disease.
Writing in the journal
Nature Medicine
, Hansson and colleagues reported how they found fragments of tau, called eMTBR-tau243, could be detected in blood and correlated with a build-up of tau tangles in the brains of people with Alzheimer’s, but not other diseases.
The team’s analyses, which involved 902 participants, found levels of this tau fragment were elevated in people with Alzheimer’s symptoms who had mild cognitive impairment, and higher again in those with dementia. Levels were not raised in people with cognitive impairments due to other conditions.
“Scientifically, these results are very promising and important as this marker performed better than existing tests and the new marker could help track performance of new drugs in trials,” said Prof Tara Spires-Jones, a neurodegeneration expert at the University of Edinburgh who was not involved in the work.
But, she said, it was not a foolproof blood test for Alzheimer’s
.
“This is also not a simple test, rather requiring complex scientific methods only available in specialist laboratories, so this will not be routinely available without further validation and development of cheaper, easier detection,” she said.
Dr Sheona Scales, the head of research at Alzheimer’s Research UK, said eMTBR-tau243 was one of a number of different biomarkers being studied for use in blood tests for Alzheimer’s.
“What’s interesting is that the blood levels of eMTBR-tau243 seem to be linked to a person’s memory and thinking abilities,” she said. “At present, it is not always possible to make a connection between the level of tangles observed with imaging and level of cognitive impairment, but having blood tests that do this will help to monitor diseases like Alzheimer’s in the brain as they progress, and help inform prognosis in future.”
Another piece of research
, also published in Nature Medicine, has revealed the ratio of two proteins in brain fluid is associated with the degree of cognitive impairment experienced by people with Alzheimer’s, independent of levels of amyloid beta plaques and tau tangles in their brains.
This research, led by scientists in the US, involved samples from 3,397 people across the US, Sweden and Finland, and looked at levels of two proteins – YWHAG and NPTX2 – that are normally found at the junctions, or synapses, between neurons in the brain.
The team found the ratio of YWHAG:NPTX2 was better able to indicate that people were experiencing cognitive problems than their levels of amyloid beta and tau, and could be used to predict their future cognitive decline and dementia onset.
Prof Tony Wyss-Coray, a co-author of the study from Stanford University, said the results could help identify the best medications for individuals and help design better clinical trials by selecting appropriate participants.

data.title: Trump's Science Policies Pose Long-Term Risk, Economists Warn
data.author: breadwinner
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：政府资助的科学研究及其长期影响和价值

不同观点：
• **os2warpman**：认为政府资助的科学研究（如Gila怪物毒液研究）虽然看似无用，但最终可能带来重大医学突破（如Exenatide的开发）。他批评一些人无法理解长期研究的价值，或者因为不喜欢这种长时间的研究过程而试图破坏。他强调，美国之所以富有，部分原因是政府对科学研究的持续资助，尽管这些研究可能需要几十年才能见到成效。

• **quux**：分享了一篇关于特朗普经济政策的文章，但没有直接表达观点，而是引导读者参考该文章。文章内容可能涉及对科学研究领域失去领先地位的担忧。

• **breadwinner**：引用文章指出，美国在人工智能（AI）领域的主导地位得益于美国大学的基础研究工作。然而，目前对在科学领域失去领先地位的担忧加剧，尤其是在AI技术可能推动未来生产力发展的背景下。

• **duxup**：批评特朗普对于长期经济和环境政策的漠不关心，认为他只关注个人短期利益，而不在乎政策对未来的影响，甚至在政策实施期间只要不影响他个人，他就不关心后果。

补充讨论：
• **长期研究的价值**：os2warpman强调基础科学研究需要长时间才能见效，但其潜在价值巨大。他以Exenatide的开发为例，说明看似无用的研究可能带来重大医学突破。

• **政治人物的态度**：duxup批评特朗普对长期政策结果的漠不关心，这与os2warpman对某些人无法理解长期研究价值的批评相呼应。

• **美国在科技领域的领先地位**：breadwinner和quux引用的文章都提到美国在科学研究和AI领域的领先地位，以及对失去这种领先地位的担忧。

争议焦点：
• **短期利益与长期研究的价值**：os2warpman和duxup的观点反映了短期利益和长期研究价值之间的矛盾，特别是当政治领导人如特朗普表现出对长期后果的漠不关心时。

• **政府资助科学研究的必要性**：os2warpman认为政府资助的研究至关重要，而duxup则指出政治领导人的短视可能威胁这种长期研究的持续性。

data.title: FBI raids home of prominent computer scientist who has gone incommunicado
data.author: JaimeThompson
data.article_summary: 著名计算机科学家王晓峰（Xiaofeng Wang）及其妻子马妮莉（Nianli Ma）的个人信息被印第安纳大学删除，他们的住所也遭到FBI突袭搜查，原因不明。王晓峰在加密技术、隐私和网络安全领域有超过20年的研究，并曾担任印第安纳大学信息、计算与工程学院的研究副院长。近期，他的邮箱、电话及个人主页被校方移除，其妻子的校方页面也被删除。FBI对其两处房产进行了搜查，但未透露搜查原因或是否有人被拘留。事件引发同行关注，有教授表示这种情况极不正常。目前，王晓峰夫妇下落不明，校方和FBI未提供更多信息。

A prominent computer scientist who has spent 20 years publishing academic papers on cryptography, privacy, and cybersecurity has gone incommunicado, had his professor profile, email account, and phone number removed by his employer, Indiana University, and had his homes raided by the FBI. No one knows why.
Xiaofeng Wang has a long list of prestigious titles. He was the associate dean for research at Indiana University's
Luddy School of Informatics, Computing and Engineering
, a fellow at the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers and the American Association for the Advancement of Science, and a tenured professor at Indiana University at Bloomington. According to his employer, he has served as principal investigator on research projects totaling nearly $23 million over his 21 years there.
He has also co-authored scores of academic papers on a diverse range of research fields, including cryptography, systems security, and data privacy, including the protection of human genomic data. I have personally spoken to him on three occasions for articles
here
,
here
, and
here
.
“None of this is in any way normal”
In recent weeks, Wang's email account, phone number, and
profile page
at the Luddy School were quietly erased by his employer. Over the same time, Indiana University also removed a profile for his wife,
Nianli Ma
, who was listed as a Lead Systems Analyst and Programmer at the university's Library Technologies division.
As reported by the
Bloomingtonian
and later the
Herald-Times
in Bloomington, a small fleet of unmarked cars driven by government agents descended on the Bloomington home of Wang and Ma on Friday. They spent most of the day going in and out of the house and occasionally transferred boxes from their vehicles. TV station WTHR, meanwhile,
reported
that a second home owned by Wang and Ma and located in Carmel, Indiana, was also searched. The station said that both a resident and an attorney for the resident were on scene during at least part of the search.
Attempts to locate Wang and Ma have so far been unsuccessful. An Indiana University spokesman didn't answer emailed questions asking if the couple was still employed by the university and why their profile pages, email addresses, and phone numbers had been removed. The spokesman provided the contact information for a spokeswoman at the FBI's field office in Indianapolis. In an email, the spokeswoman wrote: "The FBI conducted court authorized law enforcement activity at homes in Bloomington and Carmel Friday. We have no further comment at this time."
Searches of federal court dockets turned up no documents related to Wang, Ma, or any searches of their residences. The FBI spokeswoman didn't answer questions seeking which US district court issued the warrant and when, and whether either Wang or Ma is being detained by authorities. Justice Department representatives didn't return an email seeking the same information. An email sent to a personal email address belonging to Wang went unanswered at the time this post went live. Their resident status (e.g. US citizens or green card holders) is currently unknown.
Fellow researchers took to social media over the weekend to register their concern over the series of events.
"None of this is in any way normal," Matthew Green, a professor specializing in cryptography at Johns Hopkins University,
wrote
on Mastodon. He
continued
: "Has anyone been in contact? I hear he’s been missing for two weeks and his students can’t reach him. How does this not get noticed for two weeks???"
In the same thread, Matt Blaze, a McDevitt professor of computer science and law at Georgetown University,
said
: "It's hard to imagine what reason there could be for the university to scrub its website as if he never worked there. And while there's a process for removing tenured faculty, it takes more than an afternoon to do it."
Local news outlets reported the agents spent several hours moving boxes in an out of the residences. WTHR provided the following details about the raid on the Carmel home:
Neighbors say the agents announced "FBI, come out!" over a megaphone.
A woman came out of the house holding a phone. A video from a neighbor shows an agent taking that phone from her. She was then questioned in the driveway before agents began searching the home, collecting evidence and taking photos.
A car was pulled out of the garage slightly to allow investigators to access the attic.
The woman left the house before 13News arrived. She returned just after noon accompanied by a lawyer. The group of ten or so investigators left a few minutes later.
The FBI would not say what they were looking for or who is under investigation. A bureau spokesperson issued a statement: “I can confirm we conducted court-authorized activity at the address in Carmel today. We have no further comment at this time

data.title: A deliberate practice app for guitar players who want to level up
data.author: adityaathalye
data.article_summary: Captrice是一款专为吉他玩家设计的练习应用，通过智能节拍器捕捉数据并提供可操作的练习建议，专注于速度、耐力、准确性和适应性。它无需音乐理论知识，提供练习库或自定义练习功能，免费使用，无广告和注册。应用可在任何浏览器上运行，数据存储在用户设备上，支持离线模式。主要功能包括节拍器、练习构建器、 tablature/乐谱嵌入、练习库、进度洞察和分享功能。Captrice旨在帮助用户每天有效练习，提升速度，针对弱点进行训练，适合各水平玩家。该应用由软件工程师兼吉他爱好者Vineet Naik开发，未来计划推出高级功能，但基础版将始终免费。

A
deliberate
practice app
for guitar players who want to level up
Practice using a smart metronome that captures metrics and

practice method focusing on speed, endurance, accuracy, and
adaptability.

playing.

?
Features

shortcuts while playing guitar

Tablature/Notation

Library

Insights
Track your progress and get actionable insights through

Sharing

daily

them daily. Let the practice streaks chart fuel your motivation.

speed

speed while keeping track of how long you can consistenly
maintain speed and accuracy.

weak spots

create your own based on a tutorial video that works for you.

game-changing practice framework
focusing on speed, endurance, accuracy, and adaptability.
Read more

required

local-first
app that stores all data in your browser.
That means your data is truly
your
data!
Export any time. Delete any time.
Give it a try
Pricing
It's
free
!
Captrice is a "passion project".
While there are plans to offer premium features at a price,
the "no-signup, local-only" version of this app is free and I intend to keep it that way.
If you'd like to support,
buy me a coffee
or help spread the word.
It means a lot to me! ð
Why
I built captrice?
If you have 30 minutes of free time, would you pick up your
guitar or phone? The path of least resistence always wins!
Even if you picked the guitar, you'd probably noodle away
instead of practicing something that advances your skills.
The challenge isn't finding what to practice—today,
exercises are everywhere—it's choosing practice over the
endless distractions we have at our fingertips.
I built this app to solve my own struggle - curated exercises
eliminate indecision about what to pratice, the metronome keeps
me focused, and data visualizations helps with motivation.
It works for me and it might work for you too.

.

email

show email
.

to the newsletter

reach out. You will get notified about feature releases and new exercise

No spam, I promise!

data.title: Go Optimization Guide
data.author: jedeusus
data.article_summary:
《Go应用性能优化系列》是一组技术文章，旨在帮助开发者编写更快速、高效的Go应用。该系列提供实用模式、真实案例及底层性能洞察，涵盖高吞吐量API、微服务和分布式系统的优化。虽然Go的性能调优选项不如C++或Rust多，但仍有许多方法能显著提升应用性能，包括内存重用、分配控制、高效网络及并发模式。

目前文章涵盖的性能模式包括：
1. 有效使用`sync.Pool`
2. 避免不必要的内存分配
3. 结构布局与内存对齐
4. 高效错误处理
5. 零成本抽象的接口
6. 就地排序与切片重用

后续将深入探讨高性能网络，包括`net/http`和`net.Conn`的高效使用、并发连接管理、性能调优及负载测试技术。该系列适合后端工程师、对延迟敏感系统的开发者及迁移到Go的团队。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Go语言中的GC优化和内存管理策略

不同观点：
• nopurpose认为，减少GC时间的关键是避免长生命周期的分配，短生命周期的分配对GC时间影响很小。尽管任何分配都会触发更早的GC，但在实际应用中，优化GC标记阶段的时间比完全避免GC更实际。
• roundup补充了相关资源链接，并提到希望有工具能帮助在不同语言项目之间切换时记住优化要点。
• neillyons对需要进行如此细致优化的应用场景表示好奇，例如结构体字段对齐等优化。
• kevmo314强调了零拷贝技术的重要性，认为虽然需要精心设计，但收益很大，特别是在减少内存分配和移动方面。
• jrockway分享了GOMEMLIMIT在生产和CI环境中的实用性，特别是在避免内存不足问题上的帮助。
• jensneuse指出使用sync.Pool有时会产生误导，虽然pprof显示无分配，但实际内存使用可能很高，强调了测量实际效益的重要性。
• nikolayasdf123建议将现有的优化建议发展成一个社区驱动的Go优化资源，并提出在网站上直接编辑和评论的功能。
• _345询问是否有类似针对Python 3的资源。
• parhamn对sync包是否会引入泛型表示关注。
• ljm认为过度优化违背了Go语言作为简单而强大的网络服务接口的设计初衷。

补充讨论：
• EdwardDiego对Go语言在结构体对齐方面与C语言的相似性表示惊讶。
• 总体来看，讨论中涉及了GC优化、零拷贝技术、内存管理工具和包的泛型化等多个方面的技术细节和应用场景。争议焦点主要在于优化策略的选择和实际效益的测量。

43539585.article_content:
Patterns and Techniques for Writing High-Performance Applications with Go
¶
The
Go App Optimization Series
is a collection of technical articles aimed at helping developers write faster, more efficient Go applications. Whether you're building high-throughput APIs, microservices, or distributed systems, this series offers practical patterns, real-world use cases, and low-level performance insights to guide your optimization efforts.
While Go doesn’t expose as many knobs for performance tuning as languages like C++ or Rust, it still provides
plenty of opportunities
to make your applications significantly faster. From memory reuse and allocation control to efficient networking and concurrency patterns, Go offers a pragmatic set of tools for writing high-performance code.
We focus on
concrete techniques
with
mesurable impact
you can apply immediately—covering everything from core language features to advanced networking strategies.
What’s Covered So Far
¶
Common Go Patterns for Performance
¶
In this first article, we explore a curated set of high-impact performance patterns every Go developer should know:
Using
sync.Pool
effectively
Avoiding unnecessary allocations
Struct layout and memory alignment
Efficient error handling
Zero-cost abstractions with interfaces
In-place sorting and slices reuse
Each pattern is grounded in practical use cases, with benchmarks and examples you can copy into your own codebase.
What’s Coming Next
¶
High-Performance Networking in Go
¶
In our upcoming deep dive into networking, we'll focus on building high-throughput network services with Go’s standard library and beyond. This includes:
Efficient use of
net/http
and
net.Conn
Managing large volumes of concurrent connections
Performance tuning with epoll/kqueue and
GOMAXPROCS
Load testing techniques and bottleneck diagnostics
TBD...
We'll also explore when to drop down to lower-level libraries like
fasthttp
, and how to balance performance with maintainability.
Who This Is For
¶
This series is ideal for:
Backend engineers optimizing Go services in production
Developers working on latency-sensitive systems
Teams migrating to Go and building performance-critical paths
Anyone curious about Go’s performance model and trade-offs
Stay tuned—more articles, code samples, and tools are on the way. You can bookmark this page to follow the series as it evolves.

data.title: The Guardian flourishes without a paywall
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 《卫报》美国分部通过读者捐款支持其无付费墙的新闻模式，近年来取得了显著成功。在许多媒体因亿万富翁所有者的影响而面临编辑独立性问题时，《卫报》强调其没有受富人或企业压力的优势，专注于公正和准确的报道。自特朗普时代以来，《卫报》的筹款呼吁变得更加紧迫，尤其在《华盛顿邮报》和《洛杉矶时报》对卡玛拉·哈里斯撤回预期背书后，其捐款大幅增加。2024年总统选举周成为其美国读者收入历史上的最高峰。目前，《卫报》美国分部的读者捐款占总收入的60%以上，预计今年将达4400万美元，比去年增长33%。尽管曾面临亏损和重组，但在疫情期间及之后，其读者群显著增长，月访问量达4000万至5000万，甚至超过了《华尔街日报》在美国的受众规模。这种无付费墙模式的成功引发了业界对新闻商业模式创新的新思考。

43511529.article_content:
Photo-Illustration: Intelligencer; Photos: Getty Images
There was a time in media when having a billionaire owner was an asset. For many outlets, this is still the case, particularly those publishing
super-secretive group chats
of powerful government officials who seem eager to trample on the rights of the press. But for others, like the Washington
Post
and the Los Angeles
Times
, both of which have seen their benefactors bend a knee to Donald Trump and sacrifice the integrity of their newspapers in the process, ownership has become a problem. A problem that the
Guardian
US, the American arm of the British newspaper, has exploited.
“All around us, media organizations have begun to capitulate,” editor Betsy Reed writes in the current fundraising appeal at the bottom of each
Guardian
article. “
The Guardian
has neither a self-interested billionaire owner nor profit-seeking corporate henchmen pressuring us to appease the rich and powerful. With the new administration boasting about its desire to punish journalists, and Trump and his allies already pursuing lawsuits against newspapers whose stories they don’t like, it has never been more urgent, or more perilous, to pursue fair, accurate reporting. Can you support
The Guardian
today?”
The asks themselves are not new.
The Guardian
for the past eight years has asked readers to donate in support of its journalism, a “reader revenue” program that helps the paper exist without a paywall. But the appeals have gotten more strident — and more Trump-focused — since the
Post
and the L.A.
Times
withdrew expected endorsements for Kamala Harris last fall, and to great effect. The last week in February was the second-biggest week in U.S. reader-revenue history for
The Guardian
; the biggest was the week of the 2024 presidential election.
The
Guardian
US expects to hit $44 million in voluntary reader donations in the U.S. and Canada this year, up 33 percent over last year, with some people supporting on a recurring basis and others giving one-time contributions. A
first-person account
by a Canadian citizen detained by ICE, for example, netted $105,000 in pledged donations. These contributions account for more than 60 percent of the American operation’s total revenue, which last year exceeded costs by $16 million (the rest of its revenue comes from advertising and philanthropic support from foundations). The amount that people are contributing on a pledged basis doubled in October — the month that Jeff Bezos pulled the
Post
’s endorsement for Harris — and has stayed at that level every month since, according to internal data provided by
The Guardian
, which just surpassed 350,000 recurring supporters in the U.S.
“Our messaging does appeal to people to support our work as a kind of cause, and I think that works for a number of reasons,” Reed said in a recent interview in her downtown office, “but one is that there is a real crisis of access to reliable information for people who don’t want or have the means to subscribe to the New York
Times
. That is a real problem that we have an answer to.”
Guardian
managing director Steve Sachs added that
The Guardian

43511529.article_summary: 《卫报》美国分部通过读者捐款支持其无付费墙的新闻模式，近年来取得了显著成功。在许多媒体因亿万富翁所有者的影响而面临编辑独立性问题时，《卫报》强调其没有受富人或企业压力的优势，专注于公正和准确的报道。自特朗普时代以来，《卫报》的筹款呼吁变得更加紧迫，尤其在《华盛顿邮报》和《洛杉矶时报》对卡玛拉·哈里斯撤回预期背书后，其捐款大幅增加。2024年总统选举周成为其美国读者收入历史上的最高峰。目前，《卫报》美国分部的读者捐款占总收入的60%以上，预计今年将达4400万美元，比去年增长33%。尽管曾面临亏损和重组，但在疫情期间及之后，其读者群显著增长，月访问量达4000万至5000万，甚至超过了《华尔街日报》在美国的受众规模。这种无付费墙模式的成功引发了业界对新闻商业模式创新的新思考。

data.title: KOReader: Open-Source eBook Reader
data.author: charleshan
data.article_summary: KOReader是一款支持多种文档格式的电子书阅读应用，适用于Cervantes、Kindle、Kobo、PocketBook和Android设备。它支持固定页面格式（如PDF、DjVu）和重排电子书格式（如EPUB、FB2），并集成了Calibre、Wallabag、Wikipedia等服务。KOReader专为电子墨水屏设备优化，具有无动画的自定义UI、分页菜单和可调对比度。该应用高度可扩展，通过插件实现额外功能，并且在一些旧设备上具有更快的翻页速度。KOReader由全球志愿者开发和维护，支持通过Liberapay捐赠。主要功能包括多语言界面、自定义排版选项、在线词典查询和OTA更新等。安装步骤和开发指南可在其官网和Wiki上找到。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：KOReader的功能、使用体验、技术细节及相关问题

不同观点：
• II2II认为KOReader在用户界面和阅读体验方面进步显著，特别是有详细的阅读跟踪功能，对于技术书籍的阅读非常实用。同时，PDF处理功能强大，尽管eInk屏幕有局限性，KOReader通过各种设置尽量优化了阅读体验。
• OuterVale非常喜爱KOReader，并提到它可以在Kindle上使用，甚至可以通过越狱在较新的型号上安装。虽然Android版本存在一些bug，但在Kindle上的体验非常好。
• deng指出KOReader具有高度的可 hack性，大部分代码使用Lua编写，添加新功能相对容易。
• sodality2赞赏KOReader的自定义功能和与OPDB索引、自托管calibre-web的集成，使其无需USB或Amazon的服务即可传输书籍。
• arkx提到KOReader不支持纵向文本和从右到左的阅读（如日文），这是一个长期存在的问题，并引用了相关的GitHub issue和W3C标准。
• fisian询问哪里可以购买无DRM的书籍以在KOReader上阅读。
• E39M5S62提到在Kobo Libra 2上打开大文件的加载时间较长，更改字体大小也会导致较大的延迟，而内置软件则没有这些问题。
• philips期待KOReader的macOS版本，并提到在多个设备上的使用体验，尽管有些小问题，但整体功能足够好。
• jtmoulia希望KOReader能与OverDrive集成，以便阅读图书馆的电子书，但目前似乎不支持DRM书籍。
• ValtteriL认为KOReader使其Kindle重获新生，经过配置后使用非常方便，特别是前光开关功能。
• totetsu分享了在Kobo上使用KOReader的多年经验，赞赏其RSS feeds和与Calibre的集成。
• mmooss询问e-ink屏幕在电子书阅读中的独特挑战，其他用户提到屏幕刷新速度慢、对比度和色彩表现等问题。
• beAroundHere在越狱Kindle时发现了KOReader，认为其UI非常适合e-ink屏幕，虽然在Android上的体验稍逊，但仍完全可用。
• SheinH高度赞扬KOReader，特别提到其在处理EPUB和PDF文件方面的优势。
• locusofself想尝试KOReader，但担心越狱会损坏其珍贵的Kindle Oasis第二版。

补充讨论：
• KOReader的功能强大但复杂，对于新手用户可能有一定的学习曲线。
• 支持格式广泛和高度自定义是KOReader的重要优势。
• 长期存在的技术问题（如对纵向文本和右至左阅读的支持）是部分用户关注的焦点。
• 越狱和安装KOReader的过程对一些用户来说可能存在风险，特别是对于不再销售的设备型号。

KOReader is a document viewer primarily aimed at e-ink readers.
Download
•
User guide
•
Wiki
•
Developer docs
Main features
portable
: runs on embedded devices (Cervantes, Kindle, Kobo, PocketBook, reMarkable), Android and Linux computers. Developers can run a KOReader emulator in Linux and MacOS.
multi-format documents
: supports fixed page formats (PDF, DjVu, CBT, CBZ) and reflowable e-book formats (EPUB, FB2, Mobi, DOC, RTF, HTML, CHM, TXT). Scanned PDF/DjVu documents can also be reflowed with the built-in K2pdfopt library.
ZIP files
are also supported for some formats.
full-featured reading
: multi-lingual user interface with a highly customizable reader view and many typesetting options. You can set arbitrary page margins, override line spacing and choose external fonts and styles. It has multi-lingual hyphenation dictionaries bundled into the application.
integrated
with
calibre
(search metadata, receive ebooks wirelessly, browse library via OPDS),
Wallabag
,
Wikipedia
,
Google Translate
and other content providers.
optimized for e-ink devices
: custom UI without animation, with paginated menus, adjustable text contrast, and easy zoom to fit content or page in paged media.
extensible
: via plugins
fast
: on some older devices, it has been measured to have less than half the page-turn delay as the built in reading software.
and much more
: look up words with StarDict dictionaries / Wikipedia, add your own online OPDS catalogs and RSS feeds, over-the-air software updates, an FTP client, an SSH server, …
Please check the
user guide
and the
wiki
to discover more features and to help us document them.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网络文件系统在macOS等系统上的实现和改进

不同观点：
• [schmidtleonard] 认为，经过20年时间，希望新的网络文件系统实现能够解决macOS在网络延迟时卡顿的问题。这暗示当前的实现存在明显缺陷，尤其是在处理网络不稳定的情况下。

• [mrpippy] 指出，macOS、iOS和iPadOS其实已经内部使用这项技术多年，主要用于实现一些辅助文件系统（如FAT）。但直到macOS 15.4，这项技术才首次作为支持的API对第三方开放。这表明系统本身早已具备一定的技术基础，只是之前未对外公开。

• [leohonexus] 对新技术开放表示欢迎，并提到希望减少对macFUSE的依赖。macFUSE目前无人维护，且安装和使用都比较麻烦，因此新的API可能带来更好的用户体验。

补充讨论：
• [schmidtleonard] 提出的网络延迟问题是一个重要的用户痛点，可能反映出当前网络文件系统在处理不稳定网络环境时的不足。

• [mrpippy] 的回应揭示了这项技术其实早已存在，只是未被广泛应用或公开，这可能缓解了一些对技术成熟度的担忧。

• [leohonexus] 提到了第三方工具macFUSE的维护问题，这表明在实际应用中，用户对现有解决方案并不满意，期待官方的替代方案。

争议焦点：当前的网络文件系统实现是否足够成熟和稳定，能否解决实际使用中的卡顿问题。用户对macFUSE的依赖和不满也反映出对更好解决方案的迫切需求。

data.article_summary: 前GCHQ实习生哈桑·阿尔沙德（Hasaan Arshad）承认违反《计算机滥用法》，将绝密数据从安全电脑转移到手机并带回家，危害国家安全。2022年8月24日，他将手机带入GCHQ绝密区域，连接工作站并传输数据。9月22日，警方逮捕了他并搜查其住所。阿尔沙德还承认在2022年9月7日至23日期间制作儿童不雅照片。法官麦高恩（McGowan）将判决推迟至6月13日，并要求提交量刑前报告，同时保释阿尔沙德，但禁止他访问暗网。她警告称，不排除判处监禁。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GCHQ实习生的背景审查及其潜在安全风险

不同观点：
• ctippett认为，文章中对于Arshad此前承认制作儿童不雅照片的指控仅在最后几段提及，令人感到意外，并质疑GCHQ对实习生的背景审查是否充分。这暗示了对高敏感度岗位背景调查的担忧。

• Havoc对此表示震惊，质疑一个曾有前科的实习生如何能够接触到绝密信息，并将此事与之前发生的"DOGE实习生"事件相比较，暗示对GCHQ在人员筛选和信息安全管理上的质疑。

补充讨论：
• 提到"DOGE实习生"事件，可能是指过去发生过的类似安全漏洞，增加了对当前事件的批评力度，并暗示相关机构在管理上可能存在一贯的疏忽。

• 讨论中的一个焦点是，高敏感度机构如GCHQ在招聘实习生时是否进行了足够的背景调查，以及这些实习生是否真的能够接触到敏感信息。

43541160.article_content:
GCHQ worker admits taking top secret data home
13 hours ago
Share
Save
Ewan Gawne
BBC News, Manchester
Share
Save
GCHQ
GCHQ is based in Cheltenham, Gloucestershire
A former GCHQ intern has admitted risking national security by taking top secret data home with him on his mobile phone.
Hasaan Arshad, 25, pleaded guilty to an offence under the Computer Misuse Act on what would have been the first day of his trial at the Old Bailey in London.
The charge related to committing an unauthorised act which risked damaging national security.
Arshad, from Rochdale in Greater Manchester, is said to have transferred sensitive data from a secure computer to his phone, which he had taken into a top secret area of GCHQ on 24 August 2022.
Top secret is the classification for the government's most sensitive information.
The compromise of this data might cause widespread loss of life or threaten the security or economic wellbeing of the country or friendly nations, according to Ministry of Justice security guidance.
'Recklessness'
A senior judge previously ruled that some parts of Arshad's case would be heard behind closed doors, in the absence of the press and public.
The court heard that Arshad took his work mobile into a top secret GCHQ area and connected it to work station.
He then transferred sensitive data from a secure, top secret computer to the phone before taking it home, it was claimed.
Arshad then transferred the data from the phone to a hard drive connected to his personal home computer.
He was arrested and his home was searched on 22 September 2022.
Arshad's lawyer Nina Grahame KC told the court that he had admitted the offence on the "basis of recklessness".
The court was told Arshad had previously admitted two charges of making an indecent photograph of a child in relation to a number of images found between 7 and 23 September 2022.
Mrs Justice McGowan adjourned sentencing for all the charges to June 13.
The senior judge ordered a pre-sentence report and granted Arshad continued bail with various conditions, including not to access the dark web.
She told him: "I want you to understand because of your age I am making the request for the pre-sentence report in this case, but that does not mean there will not be a custodial sentence."
Arshad wore a dark grey suit, white shirt and dark brown tie and nodded that he understood before leaving the dock.

data.title: Aim: Supercharged open-source experiment tracker
data.author: karma_daemon
data.article_summary: Aim 是一个开源、自托管的机器学习实验追踪工具，能够处理上万次训练运行，提供高效美观的用户界面以比较和观察训练数据，并通过API进行编程访问。它支持与多种流行ML框架的集成，如Pytorch、TensorFlow、Hugging Face等，并允许通过SDK对元数据进行查询。Aim 还提供实时监控、日志记录、运行分组和详细调试信息，帮助用户有效组织和管理实验。此外，Aim 提供内置转换器，方便从其他实验追踪工具（如TensorBoard、MLflow）迁移日志数据。Aim 的目标是让AI开发工具更普及。

ℹ️ About
Aim is an open-source, self-hosted ML experiment tracking tool designed to handle 10,000s of training runs.
Aim provides a performant and beautiful UI for exploring and comparing training runs.
Additionally, its SDK enables programmatic access to tracked metadata — perfect for automations and Jupyter Notebook analysis.

data.title: My Book's Pre-Sale Just Barely Succeeded
data.author: hyperbrainer
data.article_summary: 作者正在撰写一本名为《Refactoring English: Effective Writing for Software Developers》的书，为避免写完后无人购买，他通过Kickstarter进行了一个月的预售，目标是5000美元，否则项目将取消。在预售的大部分时间里，销售停滞，离目标还有2000美元差距，作者几乎以为项目失败。然而，最后他幸运地在Hacker News上发布的一篇文章带来了转机，成功达到了6000美元的预售额，超出目标。尽管起初通过邮件列表和博客宣传效果不佳，但最终通过再次利用之前受欢迎的文章实现了目标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kickstarter作为市场测试工具的作用及其演变

不同观点：
• [stevage的观点] 起初使用Kickstarter是为了测试书籍市场的需求，但随着项目推进，Kickstarter本身变成了目标，所有的努力都集中在确保其成功上。这让人质疑，最终是否还能从中学到有关书籍市场需求的有用信息。换句话说，Kickstarter的成功可能更多反映了众筹活动的有效性，而非书籍市场的真实需求。

• [sadmanca的观点] 欣赏开发者博客中的故事，尤其是关于如何在Hacker News上取得成功与失败的经历。从这个角度看，Kickstarter的过程本身和其中的故事是有价值的，而不仅仅是为了测试市场需求。

补充讨论：
• Kickstarter的角色转变：从市场测试工具转变为项目的主要目标，可能导致对最初市场测试目的的偏离。
• 成功的多重因素：Kickstarter的成功可能受到多种因素的影响，如营销策略和社区参与，这些因素可能无法直接反映书籍市场的实际需求。
• 故事的价值：对于某些读者来说，项目过程中的经验和故事分享可能比单纯的市场测试结果更有吸引力。

争议焦点：Kickstarter的成功是否还能有效反映书籍市场的真实需求，或者其成功更多是其他因素的结果。

43539216.article_content:
For the past few months, I’ve been working on a book called
Refactoring English: Effective Writing for Software Developers
.
I didn’t want to spend a year writing the book only to find out that nobody wants to buy it, so I ran a one-month pre-sale on Kickstarter. I structured the project so that if I didn’t hit $5k in pre-orders, the project would be canceled, and I’d walk away with nothing.
Over the weekend, I hit my goal. As of this writing, I’ve reached $6,000 in pre-orders from 174 customers with eight hours remaining in the sale. It looks like I hit my goal comfortably.
In reality, for most of the month, I thought the book had failed, and I felt embarrassed about how poorly the pre-sale had gone.
Here’s what pre-orders looked like just four days ago:
Sales had long since plateaued. I’d already exhausted every idea I had for finding customers, and I was still $2,000 from my goal.
The thing that saved me was a lucky post on Hacker News.
Before the pre-sale
🔗︎
I started working on
Refactoring English
back in 2021. But then my business grew unexpectedly, and I spent so much time managing that company that I
never had time to work on the book
.
Until 2025, all I had of the book was a rough table of contents and a signup form for email updates about the book.
This year, I started working on the book again, and I published a couple of
sample chapters
. I heard positive feedback from readers, but I wasn’t sure if any developers would pay to read a book about improving their writing skills.
At the beginning of March, I decided the best way to see if this book was worth writing would be to do a one-month pre-sale of the book. I created a Kickstarter project for the book and let people pre-order the book for $25.
I set the project goal at $5k. I figured that would mean about 150 pre-orders plus some generous readers signing up for premium tiers to support the project.
My underwhelming first blog post
🔗︎
I wanted to launch the pre-orders on Kickstarter right after I published a new sample chapter. I hoped the blog post would be popular, and then readers would get to the end of the post and see that I’m working on a book and think, “I like this guy’s ideas so much that I’d pay $25 for more of them.”
So I published
“How to Write Useful Commit Messages”
and put a little self-ad at the bottom for the pre-sale on Kickstarter:
I added self-ads at the bottom of my sample chapters, letting readers know about the pre-sale on Kickstarter.
I emailed the book’s mailing list to share the new chapter and announce the pre-sale on Kickstarter.
1,100 people had signed up for updates about the book, but when I offered pre-orders, only 49 people ordered. That didn’t bode well. Maybe they weren’t that interested after all? Or maybe they didn’t like what I was writing?
After a week, 49 customers had pre-ordered
Refactoring English
, though this was lower than I expected given the 1,100 mailing list subscribers.
But that was okay. I still had other ideas for marketing my book.
My secret weapon
🔗︎
Even though my book’s pre-sale started slower than I’d hoped, I secretly had an ace up my sleeve.
A month earlier, I’d written a blog post called
“My Seventh Year as a Bootstrapped Founder.”
I
submitted it to Hacker News
, and it immediately shot to the #1 position on the front page. It had 45 upvotes and was growing quickly.
Sadly, within minutes, the Hacker News moderators removed my post.
I reached out to the Hacker News moderators, and they explained that I had submitted my annual retrospective too soon after my previous post,
“Lessons from my First Exit.”
They felt like the content was too similar, but I was welcome to try again after there had been two or three months of distance from the previous post.
The moderator’s decision was a bit odd because the two posts don’t overlap much, and it had
already
been two months between posts. But I find Hacker News moderation extremely fair overall, so I figured I’d just wait a month.
So, now, the moderators removing my post actually worked in my favor because it effectively meant I had a post that I knew would succeed on Hacker News, and I could submit it whenever I wanted. I could submit it during the pre-sale for my book and attract readers interested in pre-ordering.
I was excited to use this blog post to attract a new surge of attention to my book. But then I submitted it again, and it barely made a blip. It got one upvote and no comments.
I tried again on a weekend, as there’s less competition then, and it didn’t even get a single upvote.
How could Hacker News love this post so much in February and then completely ignore it a few weeks later?
No longer my favorite git commit
🔗︎
But I had another idea. There was a blog post called
“My Favourite Git Commit”
that was popular on
Hacker News
and
the /r/programming subreddit
. While I was writing “How to Write Useful Commit Messages,” I had an insight about that post that hadn’t been part of the conversation before, so I thought that would
make a g

• PostOnce认为吉卜力艺术的美在于其动态表现和情感共鸣，AI生成艺术无法复制这种深度。他提到即使有模仿者，吉卜力的独特性依然不可替代，并引用Doom游戏的例子来类比。同时，他指出吉卜力曾面临类似竞争（如Studio Ponoc），但这并未削弱其价值。
• knowknow担心吉卜力风格被机器复制可能会违背其艺术初衷，并可能引发法律问题，尤其是如果AI模型使用了吉卜力电影作为训练数据。他认为原艺术家可能会对此感到不快。
• Havoc指出Google的重大升级和吉卜力风格在社交媒体上的流行，并认为在不同平台上这些话题的关注度不同。
• keyle关注消费者产品发布时技术优越性与文化影响之间的不对等关系，认为吸引注意力的往往是独特的氛围而非技术指标。
• margorczynski对AI生成信息图表的实用性表示赞赏，认为这为无2D动画知识的人提供了制作演示文稿等内容的可能性，尤其是文本的准确性带来了许多新机会。
• ungreased0675直指大规模的版权侵权问题。
• m3kw9认为吉卜力风格的AI生成图片只是一时的流行，初看有吸引力，但很快会让人失去兴趣。

• shmerl引用宫崎骏的观点，强烈反对这种AI生成艺术，认为这是对生命的侮辱。
• tehjoker认为人们能够用喜爱的风格创作是好事，虽然大多数人创作的可能只是平庸之作，但有些人能达到情感和 intellectual 的高度。他对OpenAI可能借此盈利感到不安，认为这是对他人劳动成果的剥削。
• rufus_foreman作为一个外行，询问什么是吉卜力。
• zombiwoof批评硅谷公司对艺术风格被复制的问题漠不关心，只关注利润。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI生成艺术是否侵犯了吉卜力风格的版权及其道德问题。
• 讨论还涉及技术进步与传统艺术价值之间的冲突。
• 有人担心AI生成艺术可能会削弱原创艺术的文化和经济价值。
• 对AI生成艺术的长期影响存在不同看法，有人认为只是一时流行，有人认为有实用价值。

Trump Administration To Review Billions in Federal Funding to Harvard
By
Caroline S. Engelmayer
By
Dhruv T. Patel
and
Grace E. Yoon
, Crimson Staff Writers
Updated March 31, 2025, at 5:25 p.m.
Three federal agencies announced a review of more than $8 billion in “multi-year grant commitments” to Harvard as part of an ongoing investigation into the University by the Federal Task Force to Combat Antisemitism on Monday.
The review — which was launched by the Department of Education, Department of Health and Human Services, and the United States General Services Administration — marks a drastic escalation in the Trump administration’s threats against Harvard over its response to pro-Palestine protests and alleged campus antisemitism.
The review also includes more than $255 million in contracts.
It comes weeks after the Trump administration pulled
more than $400 million
in federal funding to Columbia University, demanding in exchange that Columbia change disciplinary policies and place its Middle Eastern, African, and South Asian studies programs under administrative control.
Columbia ultimately caved to many of the demands — but the exchange resulted in massive national backlash and the abrupt ouster of the university’s interim president. Harvard, confronted with an unprecedented threat to its operations, may be forced to decide how much it is willing to concede in order to preserve its federal funding.
The public announcement of the review into Harvard’s funds did not outline specific demands but linked to a document outlining the conditions issued to Columbia.
“Harvard’s failure to protect students on campus from anti-Semitic discrimination — all while promoting divisive ideologies over free inquiry — has put its reputation in serious jeopardy,” Secretary of Education Linda McMahon wrote in the press release.
Just four days before the Trump administration pulled $400 million in federal funding, Columbia received a letter — similar to Harvard’s — saying that its federal grants and contracts were being reviewed. It is unclear whether funding cuts will follow in Harvard’s case.
Advertisement
Under the review, the Trump administration will examine individual contracts to determine whether stop-work orders should be issued. The University will also be expected to provide the White House with a list of federal contracts not included in the initial review.
A University spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
“We could not carry out our mission the way we do now without substantial federal research support, nor could we provide the benefits to the nation that we do now without that support,” Garber said in
a December interview
with The Crimson.
Harvard has spent months bracing for an unstable political future and potentially massive losses to its funding — especially after the Trump administration repeatedly
threatened research funding
. Harvard President Alan M. Garber ’76 announced a
University-wide hiring freeze
in early March, and the
Faculty of Arts and Sciences
issued budget guidance in February urging FAS leadership to keep spending flat in fiscal year 2026.
But Monday’s review puts Harvard squarely in the crosshairs of more targeted threats.
At Columbia, then-interim President Katrina Armstrong capitulated to the Trump administration’s demands within two weeks. But after Armstrong seemed to downplay the extent of Columbia’s concessions at a faculty meeting — possibly to pacify an outraged professoriate — she abruptly departed from her seat, which was filled by one of the school’s trustees.
The crisis
at Columbia illustrates that, elsewhere, top university brass have opted to trade policy concessions for a chance at leniency.
But similar moves at Harvard could ignite
backlash among faculty
who see them as compromising its academic independence. In an extraordinary show of unity, more than 600 Harvard faculty
signed a letter
urging the University’s governing boards to “refuse to comply with unlawful demands that threaten academic freedom and university self-governance.”
The
federal antisemitism task force
— which is investigating nine other schools, including Columbia —
plans to visit Harvard’s campus
but has not yet announced a date.
This is a developing story and will be updated.

data.title: Show HN: TypeScript as a proof assistant for intuitionistic propositional logic
data.author: xxmarijnw
data.article_summary: 这篇文章展示了如何使用TypeScript模拟直觉主义命题逻辑的证明助手。通过定义逻辑基本类型的编码，如`False`、`True`、`Con`（与）、`Dis`（或）、`Imp`（蕴涵）、`Iff`（双向蕴涵）和`Not`（否定），并实现相应的证明和逻辑规则，如蕴涵引入和消除、与和或的引入和消除、矛盾原理、以及一些更有趣的逻辑重言式和反证法。通过这些定义，TypeScript被用作一种证明工具，展示了如何在类型层面上实现逻辑推理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TypeScript（或类似的类型系统）中的类型检查与证明助手中的完备性与健全性问题

不同观点：
• [voidmain] 认为代码中的递归定义 (`prove_false()`) 可能导致循环证明，这在证明助手中通常通过计算的完备性来避免。他指出，TypeScript 可能存在一些更微妙的健全性问题。
• [voidmain] 提到自己不是这方面的专家，并提出一种可能性：原作者可能意图让用户不仅进行类型检查，还要执行证明函数以验证终止性。然而，他对此表示怀疑，认为在很多情况下执行这种证明可能会耗尽资源，并且可能仍然不健全。

补充讨论：
• [voidmain] 提出了对递归函数在类型系统中应用的担忧，尤其是涉及到终止性和健全性的问题。
• 评论中还暗示了证明助手的理想特性，即确保所有证明都能终止并避免循环证明，而这在 TypeScript 等语言中可能难以完全实现。
• 讨论了执行证明函数的可能性和现实性问题，指出即使执行成功也可能面临资源限制。

data.title: Ask HN: What's the best way to get started with LLM-assisted programing?
data.author: mywittyname
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕AI编程工具（如Cursor、Aider、OpenRouter等）的讨论，以及是否应该使用AI工具辅助开发。

不同观点：
• **反对使用主流AI工具（bionhoward）**：认为Perplexity和ChatGPT的规则限制了商业用途，使用这些工具等同于付费帮助他们改进模型，最终可能威胁到自己的工作。建议学习其他编程语言或使用Groq和Ollama等工具，因为它们允许保留输出数据，可以用于训练自己的模型。
• **支持Cursor工具（biotechbio）**：从实际经验出发，认为Cursor在处理特定领域任务时表现出色，特别是在机器学习等需要特定工具和方法的领域，Cursor能提供80%的帮助，且价格合理。
• **推荐Aider.chat（thuanao）**：认为Aider.chat可以在不改变开发环境的情况下实现Cursor类似的功能，适合习惯在终端工作的人。
• **质疑LLM工具的长期价值（rf15）**：认为LLM只能处理你熟悉的基础任务，过度依赖LLM可能会导致学习停滞，最终影响开发者的技能提升。
• **建议从基础开始，逐步适应工具（thebeardisred）**：推荐从简单的工具如Aider开始，先理解工具的运作原理，再逐步过渡到更复杂的工具，认为初学者需要保持对工具的掌控力。
• **偏好聊天界面和特定工具（medhir）**：认为聊天界面有助于保持思路清晰，避免一次性修改太多内容，同时对Gemini 2.5的表现表示认可。
• **推荐开源工具Dyad（willchen）**：介绍了自己开发的Dyad工具，强调其开源和与Pycharm兼容的特性，适合不想切换IDE的开发者。
• **推荐OpenRouter（rbrownmh）**：认为OpenRouter文档完善，易于上手，且提供了丰富的使用示例，适合初学者。
• **分享实际项目经验（inheritedwisdom）**：介绍了团队在VSCode中使用Cline和Sonnet 3.7的经验，强调了定义明确的架构和细化任务的重要性。
• **推荐Emacs插件（wmedrano）**：认为GPTel插件在Emacs中的表现值得关注，适合Emacs用户。
• **推荐Bolt.new（sans_souse）**：通过个人实验推荐Bolt.new，认为这是一个值得尝试的工具。
• **自定义开发工具（mpalmer）**：建议开发者根据自己的需求编写Python脚本，而不是依赖现成的AI工具，认为这样可以更好地与个人工作流对齐。
• **强烈推荐Cline（ramesh31）**：认为Cline的表现接近“魔法”，表现出色。
• **学习路径建议（kittikitti）**：建议选择一个项目并尝试使用不同的LLM工具，通过实践提升技能，而不是局限于单一工具。

补充讨论：
• **对Cursor的疑问（andrewstuart）**：请求对Cursor的优势进行总结，显示出对Cursor工具实际效果的好奇。

总体来看，讨论的焦点包括是否应该依赖AI编程工具、不同工具的优劣比较以及如何在实际项目中有效利用这些工具。

data.title: OxiCloud – lightweight alternative to Nextcloud file sharing (Rust)
data.author: sandreas
data.article_summary: OxiCloud 是一个轻量级、高效、安全的自托管云存储解决方案，采用 Rust 编写，旨在替代 NextCloud。其特点包括资源占用少、界面简洁响应快速、支持多语言、以及通过 LTO 优化性能。OxiCloud 具有简单的安装和配置过程，支持 PostgreSQL 数据库，并遵循清洁架构原则，便于功能扩展和组件替换。当前开发重点包括用户认证、文件分享、WebDAV 支持、文件版本控制和移动端优化等功能。项目遵循 MIT 许可，欢迎贡献和反馈。

A lightweight, Rust-powered alternative to NextCloud
I built OxiCloud because I wanted a simpler, faster file storage solution than existing options. After struggling with NextCloud's performance on my home server, I decided to create something that prioritizes speed and simplicity while still being robust enough for daily use.
OxiCloud's straightforward interface for file and folder management
✨ What makes OxiCloud different?
Lightweight
: Minimal resource requirements compared to PHP-based alternatives
Responsive UI
: Clean, fast interface that works well on both desktop and mobile
Rust Performance
: Built with Rust for memory safety and speed
Optimized Binary
: Uses Link Time Optimization (LTO) for maximum performance
Simple Setup
: Get running with minimal configuration
Multilingual
: Full support for English and Spanish interfaces
🛠️ Getting Started
Prerequisites
Rust 1.70+ and Cargo
PostgreSQL 13+ database
512MB RAM minimum (1GB+ recommended)
Installation
#
Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/DioCrafts/oxicloud.git
cd
oxicloud
#
Configure your database (create .env file with your PostgreSQL connection)
echo
"
DATABASE_URL=postgres://username:password@localhost/oxicloud
"
>
.env
#
Build the project
cargo build --release
#
Run database migrations
cargo run --bin migrate
#
Run the server
cargo run --release
The server will be available at
http://localhost:8085
🧩 Technical Implementation
OxiCloud follows Clean Architecture principles with clear separation of concerns:
Domain Layer
: Core business logic and entities
Application Layer
: Use cases and application services
Infrastructure Layer
: External systems and implementations
Interfaces Layer
: API and web controllers
The architecture makes it easy to extend functionality or swap components without affecting the core system.

🗺️ Roadmap
I'm actively working on improving OxiCloud with features that I need personally:
User authentication and multi-user support (in progress)
File sharing with simple links
WebDAV support for desktop integration

data.title: Is BIND9 suitable as a recursive resolver in 2025?
data.author: plagiat0r
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了在2025年使用BIND9作为完全递归DNS解析器的部署过程。作者为一家大型IT公司提供DNS培训和咨询，需要设计一个DNS基础设施，使用BIND9来满足公司产品需求。BIND9被配置为转发所有查询到上游递归解析器，但为了实现完全递归解析，还需要配置根提示区。在实际测试中，初始查询返回了SERVFAIL错误，表明解析失败。经过进一步排查，作者发现问题可能与网络配置或BIND9的缓存有关。最终，文章强调了配置递归解析器时需要注意的细节，如防火墙规则和BIND9的配置选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于BIND9在DNS解析中的表现及相关问题的分析

不同观点：
• **sybercecurity的观点**：BIND9曾经是许多DNS设备的基础，即使你没有运行自己的递归服务器，可能仍然在使用BIND，只不过通过GUI前端进行操作。这意味着BIND的影响可能比想象中更广泛。

• **jmholla的观点**：
   - 文章对BIND的批评不够公正，认为文章在没有充分解释和论证的情况下指责BIND。
   - 文章得出结论后，后续部分没有很好地支持这些结论，信息呈现不连贯。
   - 举例说明了一些BIND的配置问题，如未设置`forward only`导致的问题，并指出即使是推荐的Unbound也会有类似问题。
   - 对文章使用"annoying"一词描述IPv6问题感到不满，认为这是技术限制而非BIND的过错。
   - 认为BIND是一个基础的DNS解析器，功能简单但为其他更具功能的解析器提供了基础，仍有改进空间。

• **plagiat0r的观点**：支持文章的观点，认为BIND-9.18和BIND-9.20存在递归算法上的bug，并使用Wireshark进行了验证。

补充讨论：
• **对文章结构和写作方式的批评**：jmholla认为文章在信息组织和措辞上存在问题，如对BIND的指责不够公正，且部分信息与主旨无关。

data.title: The North Korea worker problem is bigger than you think
data.author: bentocorp
data.article_summary: 北韩技术专家已渗透全球企业，担任全职工程师等高权限职位，远超以往认知。内幕风险管理公司DTEX透露，这些渗透不仅限于短期 freelance 工作，而是深入关键基础设施，拥有管理权限，可以控制系统访问、安装软件、编写代码等。美国司法部和财政部已对相关个人和实体提起诉讼和制裁，指控北韩派出数千技术人员以虚假身份获取 freelance 工作并将收入汇回平壤。多家安全公司观察到与北韩相关的内鬼活动增加，许多企业无意中雇佣了北韩人员。这些人员迅速渗透公司网络，并通过远程工具让其他同伙参与行动。他们工作表现突出，甚至比一般员工更优秀，导致企业难以察觉异常。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：招聘过程中对技术专长的要求是否合理，特别是涉及技术出现时间与简历不一致的问题。

不同观点：
• **观点一**（隐含于评论中）：招聘要求中有时会不合理地要求应聘者具备在某技术正式发布前或广泛应用前的专业知识。这暗示了招聘方可能存在不切实际或时间错乱的期望，比如要求应聘者在某技术尚未成熟或普及前就掌握它，这是不合理的。例子：评论者提到在一些招聘启事中看到过这种现象。

• **观点二**（可能代表招聘方立场）：招聘方可能并未意识到技术发展的时间线，或者他们希望找到在技术早期阶段就有前瞻性学习能力的人。这意味着他们可能更看重候选人的自学能力和技术敏锐度，而非严格的时间顺序。这种要求可能是为了筛选出对技术趋势非常敏感的应聘者。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：招聘启事中要求应聘者在技术正式发布前就具备相关专业知识，是否属于不切实际的要求。这反映出招聘方和求职者之间对技术发展时间线的理解差异，以及对技术专长的期望不同。

• **潜在的“信号”**：评论还提到“长时间停顿”和“简历中的不一致”可能是面试中的“信号”，提示面试官应聘者可能存在夸大或不实的成分。这在招聘过程中也可能引发对应聘者诚信和能力的质疑。

North Korean nationals have infiltrated businesses across the globe with a more expansive level of organization and deep-rooted access than previously thought, insider risk management firm DTEX told CyberScoop.
This swarm of technical North Korean experts isn’t just intruding businesses as ad hoc freelance IT workers; they’ve gained full-time employment as engineers and specialists of various skill sets with the highest degree of access in enterprise systems.
“We work with a fair cross-section of the Fortune Global 2000 organizations, and right now we have active investigations going on with 7% of our customer base,” Mohan Koo, co-founder and president of DTEX, said in an interview. DTEX has a couple hundred customers and estimates thousands of critical infrastructure organizations have been infiltrated by North Korean operatives.
“Some of the roles that we’re investigating, the infiltrators that we’re investigating right now, have actually got the keys to the kingdom,” Koo said. “They have privileged-access rights. They have the ability to turn on access and turn off access for other workers. They have the ability to install and uninstall software. They have the ability to write code.”
Advertisement
DTEX’s ongoing research indicates the North Korean regime’s yearslong scheme goes much deeper than contract work and extends to roles beyond traditional IT. The Justice and Treasury Departments have issued
indictments
and
sanctioned people and entities
allegedly involved in North Korea’s effort to send thousands of specialized technical professionals outside of the country to secure freelance jobs under false pretenses and funnel their wages back to Pyongyang.
Multiple threat hunters have observed a surge of insider threat activity linked to North Korea. Adam Meyers, head of CrowdStrike’s counter adversary operations, last month said a “tremendous amount of companies” have unknowingly hired North Koreans for technical development roles.
Nearly 40% of the incident response cases CrowdStrike worked on last year involving the North Korea state-backed group it tracks as Famous Chollima were insider-threat operations. Insider threats accounted for 5% of Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 incident response cases last year, and the number of those tied to North Korea tripled in 2024.
Oftentimes, organizations unknowingly hire multiple North Korean nationals. “It’s typically not just one,” said Rob Schuett, director of insider intelligence investigations at DTEX.
“A single compromise is just the beginning,” he said. “It’s kind of like an insect infestation in your home. You see that one insect and you may be able to spray that one with chemicals and get rid of it, or move it outside. However, you know that in the walls and the cracks and the crevices there’s a bigger problem underfoot.”
Advertisement
Quick pivots, hops to other networks
Once a North Korean national is hired and starts the employment onboarding process, they move quickly to further infiltrate the organization.
They move into virtual desktop infrastructure environments, using access granted from one entity to pivot to a third party, often a trusted partner.
“That opens up the whole threat of the supply chain being infiltrated, and that’s a very, very complex problem,” Koo said.
DTEX’s investigation into insider threats backed by North Korea reached an “alarming conclusion,” Koo said, a shocking reality that the extent of known compromise is widespread and likely more prevalent than confirmed thus far.
Advertisement
“We’re only really catching the dumb ones, the ones that are making OpSec mistakes, and they’re pivoting around in places that we didn’t know were infiltrated,” Schuett said. This means, North Korean technical workers are probably operating in dozens of infiltrated organizations, including those they aren’t employed by, simultaneously.
North Korean nationals are also installing various remote access tools, which are approved for use and often blend in to typical onboarding activities, when most employees set up and gain initial access to work systems.
“They’re using a specific identity and a specific individual to gain employment, and that individual’s skill set is specifically targeted to gain employment at the organization,” Koo said. “But once they’ve gained employment, it’s just an access right, and then they use these remote tools to enable the others to do the work.”
North Koreans are doing the job — better than most
The threat posed by North Korean technical workers stands out, compared to other nation-state backed activity, because they’re doing the work companies are paying them to do. “In some cases, they’re doing a better job than most,” Koo said.

data.title: Microsoft redesigns BSOD, drops QR code, frowning face, blue colour
data.author: vo2maxer
data.article_summary: 微软正在将Windows 11中的“蓝屏死机”（BSOD）更改为“黑屏死机”（Black Screen of Death），背景变为黑色，并去掉了愁眉苦脸的表情符号。新版死机屏幕信息更少，只有简单的重启提示，与Windows更新屏幕相似，容易混淆。早期Windows 11曾试验过黑屏，但未正式发布。而在Windows Insider Program中，测试者会看到“绿屏死机”（Green Screen of Death），背景为绿色以便于调试。此次改动可能会给IT管理员带来困扰，因为他们需要更多技术信息来解决问题。新版黑屏死机将向所有Windows 11 24H2用户推出。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应该移除错误信息中的蓝色背景和其它元素（如表情符号）

不同观点：
• [HWR_14的观点] 不支持移除标志性的蓝色背景。他认为蓝色背景是具有标志性的设计元素，移除它没有必要。
• [genevra的观点] 支持移除多余的装饰元素，并认为新的改动提供了更多有用的信息，明确指出了什么失败了。虽然会怀念表情符号，但移除无关紧要的字符串是可以接受的。

补充讨论：
• genevra指出新版本的改进之处在于提供了更明确的信息，这提升了用户体验。
• 争议的焦点在于蓝色背景是否具有实际功能价值，还是仅仅是装饰性的。HWR_14认为它是标志性的，可能有情感价值，而genevra更看重信息的实际效用。
• 表情符号（如皱眉脸）虽然被认为有些多余，但也有用户对其有情感依赖，例如genevra表示会想念它。

43539926.article_content:
Home
Windows 11
Windows 11
Old/current BSOD in Windows 11
Microsoft is killing off the Blue Screen of Death… and replacing it with Black Screen of Death. It’s also dropping the frowning face for some reason, and I am not sure I like it because the updated screen doesn’t have enough information. Let me show how it’s changing in newer builds of
Windows 11 24H2
and what it means for the IT admins.
The Blue Screen of Death error is one of the familiar, although hated, screens of the Windows operating system. It’s been part of Windows since Windows 3.0, which was released in 1990, and it hasn’t really evolved since the release of modern operating systems like Windows 7 or Vista.
Old/current BSOD in Windows 11
BSOD has always looked blue, which is why it has “Blue Screen of Death” in its name.
Some early Windows 11 builds previously experimented with a “Black Screen of Death,” but that never shipped in production. Also, it wasn’t a redesign because Microsoft simply coated the Blue Screen of Death with a black background. It still had the growing face, QR code, and information about what had happened.
The Blue Screen of Death is changing and getting a black background again, but this time, it’s a proper redesign. Also, if you’re in the Windows Insider Program, you’ll have a Green Screen of Death. Everything remains the same, but background is changed to green to reflect Insider Program status, which helps in debugging.
Closer look at “Black Screen of Death” in Windows 11 24H2
New “Black Screen of Death”
The new Black Screen of Death looks very difficult. It still gives the familiar feeling that your PC has run into a problem and needs to reboot.
Windows is updating the screen | Image Courtesy: WindowsLatest.com
However, you might confuse the new BSOD with the Windows Update screen. The two screens look very similar. Perhaps, Microsoft needs to add back the frowning face to make it look less confusing.
Another noteworthy change and reason for confusion is that the new Black Screen of Death (BSOD) doesn’t show much technical information, which previously appeared in the original Blue Screen of Death error.
For example, take a look at the old/original BSOD:
BSOD
The original BSOD clearly stated that “Your PC ran into a problem and needs to restart. We’re just collecting some error info, and then we’ll restart for you.” It also included a frowning face and a QR code for you to scan and look up the information on the Internet.
On the other hand, the new BSOD simply states that “Your device ran into a problem and needs to restart.”
While it’s easier to read, it does look a lot like the Windows Update screen, as you can see in the comparison gallery below:
1
of 2
Windows is updating screen | Image Courtesy: WindowsLatest.com
Microsoft really needs to redo the Black Screen of Death to make it evident that it’s an error screen and Windows is not updating. The new redesign could make things difficult for IT admins, who typically work with beginners to fix their computer issues.
At the moment, the updated BSOD is rolling out to all testers (Windows Insider Program users) with Windows 11 24H2 or newer.
It will roll out to non-Insiders on Windows 11 24H2 in the coming weeks.

data.title: OpenAI closes $40B funding round, startup now valued at $300B
data.author: rvz
data.article_summary: OpenAI宣布完成史上最大规模的私营科技公司融资，共筹集40亿美元，使公司估值达到300亿美元。其中，软银投资30亿美元，其他投资者共投资10亿美元。这笔资金将用于推进AI研究和扩展计算基础设施，部分资金将投入与Oracle的合资项目Stargate。然而，若OpenAI未能在年底前重组为营利实体，软银的投资可能削减至10亿美元。目前，OpenAI预计今年收入将增至三倍，达127亿美元。公司还进行了高层变动，CEO Sam Altman将专注于研究和产品，运营主管将接管日常事务。此外，生成式AI市场预计在十年内营收将突破1万亿美元。

data.title: HTTP/3 and the QUIC Internet Protocol
data.author: ducaale
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了QUIC协议如何克服HTTP/2 over TCP的局限性，提升网络传输效率。HTTP/2通过多路复用改善了效率，但仍面临两个主要问题：队头阻塞（一个数据包丢失会影响所有流）和连接持久性问题（网络切换导致连接中断）。为解决这些问题，Google开发了QUIC协议。QUIC基于UDP，引入了独特的连接ID（CID），使得连接不依赖于IP地址，从而支持连接迁移。同时，QUIC在流级别处理数据包确认和重传，避免队头阻塞。此外，QUIC内置加密功能，通过单次握手同时建立连接和加密，减少延迟。QUIC握手过程通过交换连接ID和加密参数完成，进一步提升传输效率。

43536718.article_content:
In a previous article, we delved into
the TCP/IP networking model
. As the article concluded, we examined the significant advancements introduced by HTTP/2, particularly its ability to multiplex multiple requests over a single TCP connection. This approach not only enhanced efficiency but also addressed many of the limitations found in earlier protocols.
However, HTTP/2 over TCP faced two significant challenges:
Head-of-Line Blocking
: If a packet is lost in one stream, it can block the delivery of packets in all other streams sharing the same connection.
Connection Persistence
: Since TCP tracks connections using packet sequence numbers tied to specific IP addresses, switching networks (e.g., from Wi-Fi to mobile data) forces the connection to drop, requiring a complete re-establishment.
To overcome these limitations, a team at Google began developing a new protocol in 2012 called
QUIC
. The goal was to shift key features, including multiplexing, connection migration, and encryption, to the transport layer. By doing so, QUIC addresses many of the shortcomings of the older model, as we’ll explore in this article.
The QUIC Protocol
QUIC (Quick UDP Internet Connections) operates over UDP instead of TCP, offering a faster and more lightweight alternative. However, UDP lacks built-in reliability, functioning on a "fire-and-forget" basis. It simply sends packets without ensuring they arrive or tracking whether they are lost.
To overcome this limitation, QUIC incorporates its own sophisticated connection tracking and management mechanisms, providing the reliability and efficiency needed for modern internet applications.
Connection Tracking
The QUIC specifications begin by assigning a unique Connection ID (CID) to each connection. Instead of relying on source and destination IP addresses for connection tracking, the CID serves as the identifier, shared between the source and destination. Even if IP addresses change, the server uses the known CID to maintain the same connection for communication.
Consider a visitor session on a website. If the website tracks visitors by their IP address, a change in the IP address makes it appear as a different visitor. However, if both the visitor and the website use a unique session ID, the website can still recognize the visitor even if they switch networks, as long as the same session ID is shared. That’s precisely the change QUIC introduces compared to TCP.
Packet Acknowledgment and Retransmission
Like TCP, QUIC keeps track of which packets have been received and retransmits any that are lost. However, it operates at the stream level rather than the connection level.
By shifting multiplexing from the application layer to the transport layer, QUIC can monitor each stream independently. If a packet belonging to one stream is dropped, it doesn't block the entire connection. Instead, packets from other streams continue to flow uninterrupted while the transport layer focuses on retransmitting the lost packet.
This approach eliminates the head-of-line blocking problem of the TCP protocol, improving efficiency and reduces latency, especially in environments with high packet loss.
Built-in Encryption
TCP lacks built-in encryption capabilities; it simply transmits packets received from the application layer. As a result, a separate handshake is required to negotiate encryption after the TCP connection is established.
QUIC, on the other hand, handles encryption internally. This means a single handshake both initiates the connection and sets up encryption, reducing the latency involved in establishing connections.
The QUIC Handshake
Before we look into the QUIC handshake, let's take a look at the TLS/TCP handshake:

2001
// TLS Handshake
$

HELLO

XXXX

previous article
.
Now, let's investigate the QUIC handshake:

data.author: raj7desai
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI对就业市场的影响

不同观点：
• MaxHoppersGhost：认为风投（VCs）过于夸大AI对就业市场的影响。他们通常追逐和炒作趋势，因此其言论不可尽信。MaxHoppersGhost认为AI在未来一两年内不会完全取代人力。

• trod1234：认为“丰饶时代”不会如人们所想的那样到来，反而更可能是通过限制人口数量来实现的。trod1234指出，蓝领工作受AI影响较小，但入门级白领工作和支持性岗位将面临极大风险。高级职位由于任务抽象性较高相对安全，但由于劳动力管道问题，若AI取代入门级工作，未来可能会导致社会经济崩溃。

• kypro：认为AI最终会取代所有人类工作，尤其是知识型工作。他以工业革命使马匹 redundant 为例，说明AI将以更低成本完成任务，从而取代人类劳动力。不过，物理劳动由于机器人技术的限制，短期内较难被取代。

• admissionsguy：对VCs认为AI将在短期内取代人力的观点表示怀疑，指出如果相信这种说法，可以通过金融市场获利而不是担心就业问题。

• metalman：指出自动化和AI已经导致一些工作岗位减少，比如语言翻译和政府服务岗位。不过，这种自动化提高了公众参与度和税收，因此未必是坏事。

• deafpolygon：认为AI不会导致工作岗位消失，除非公司本来就有裁员计划。企业可能会放缓招聘，但不会完全停止。

• scarface_74：认为涉及利益相关者管理和实施业务价值的工作不会被AI取代，开发人员也不会被完全取代。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于AI对不同类型工作的影响程度以及其对社会经济的潜在影响。
- 讨论中提到AI对入门级职位和知识型工作的威胁，以及对高级职位和物理劳动的不同影响。
- 有人质疑VCs的动机和言论可信度，认为他们常夸大趋势以获取利益。
- 社会经济系统的脆弱性和全球化对就业市场的影响也被提及，指出过度优化和单一失败点可能导致系统性风险。

olorado regulators
are issuing licenses for providing psychedelic mushrooms and are planning to authorize the state’s first “healing centers,” where the mushrooms can be ingested under supervision, in late spring or early summer.
The dawn of state-regulated psychedelic mushrooms has arrived in Colorado, nearly two years since Oregon began offering them. The mushrooms are a Schedule I drug and illegal under federal law except for clinical research. But more than a dozen cities nationwide have deprioritized or decriminalized them in the past five years, and many eyes are turned toward Oregon’s and Colorado’s state-regulated programs.
Related
Therapeutic Psychedelics Beset by Red Tape
“In Oregon and Colorado, we’re going to learn a lot about administration of psychedelics outside of clinical, religious, and underground settings because they’re the first to try this in the U.S.,” said William R. Smith, an assistant professor of psychiatry at the University of North Carolina School of Medicine.
Psychedelic mushrooms and their psychoactive compound psilocybin have the potential to treat people with depression and anxiety, including those unresponsive to other medications or therapy.
The National Institute on Drug Abuse
, part of the National Institutes of Health, says the risk of mental health problems caused by ingesting mushrooms in a supervised clinical setting is low, but may be higher outside of a clinical setting. Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said in a social media post last year, before his nomination as U.S. health secretary, that his “mind is open to the idea of psychedelics for treatment.”
Some medical experts say
more research
is needed, particularly in people with a diagnosis or family history of psychotic or bipolar disorder. Adverse effects of psilocybin, including headache and nausea, typically resolve within
one to two days
. However, extended difficulties from using psychedelics can last weeks, months, or years; anxiety and fear, existential struggle, social disconnection, and feeling detached from oneself and one’s surroundings are
most common
. After the decriminalization and legalization in Oregon and Colorado, psychedelic mushroom exposures reported to
poison control centers
ticked up in these states and nationally.
In February, about 40 people organized by the psychedelic advocacy group the
Nowak Society
gathered in Boulder, Colorado to talk about the coming changes in the state. They included Mandy Grace, who received her state license to administer psychedelic mushrooms, and Amanda Clark, a licensed mental health counselor from Denver, who both praised the therapeutic power of mushrooms.
“You get discouraged in your practice because the current therapies are not enough for people,” Clark said.
Some medical experts say more research is needed, particularly in people with a diagnosis or family history of psychotic or bipolar disorder.
Colorado voters approved
Proposition 122
in 2022 to legalize natural psychedelics, after Oregon voters in 2020 approved legalizing psilocybin for therapeutic use. Colorado’s program is modeled after, but not the same as, Oregon’s, under which 21,246 psilocybin products have been sold as of March, a total that could include secondary doses, according to the Oregon Health Authority.
As of mid-March, Colorado
has received applications
for at least 15 healing center licenses, nine cultivation licenses, four manufacturer licenses, and one testing facility license for growing and preparing the mushrooms, under
rules developed over two years
by the governor-appointed Natural Medicine Advisory Board.
P
sychedelic treatments
in Oregon are expensive, and are likely to be so in Colorado, too, said Tasia Poinsatte, Colorado director of the nonprofit Healing Advocacy Fund, which supports state-regulated programs for psychedelic therapy. In Oregon, psychedelic mushroom sessions are typically $1,000 to $3,000, are not covered by insurance, and must be paid for up front.

data.author: nnx
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了对对话界面的质疑。尽管每隔几年就会出现新的AI技术让人们认为对话界面将成为下一计算范式，但实际上人们依然按传统方式使用电脑。对话界面依赖的自然语言在数据传输速度和准确性上存在瓶颈，人类思维速度远超语言表达速度。日常中，人类使用手势、表情等更快的交流方式。类似地，人机交互也从命令行演变为图形界面，结合键盘快捷键提升效率。作者认为，自然语言并非人机交互的终极形式，高效和便捷才是关键。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：语音用户界面（Voice UI）的效率、应用场景及其与传统用户界面的关系。

不同观点：
• [pugio的观点] 认为语音输入需要压缩以提高传输速度，类似于使用快捷键的效率。他提到希望通过简单的语音指令或声音与AI助手（如Claude）快速交互，并分享了自己通过语音界面进行编程和学习的成功经验。他还设想未来可以实时指挥AI编码并观察程序演变。
• [cdrini的观点] 同意语音UI应作为当前键盘和鼠标操作的补充，而不是替代。他引用Baddeley的工作记忆模型，认为人类的大脑对视觉和听觉信息的处理是分开的，语音UI可以在不占用视觉注意力的情况下实现多任务处理。他还指出，语言本身会随着时间自动"压缩"，例如通过使用上下文简化词汇，因此不需要特意压缩语音输入。
• [techpineapple的观点] 提出观察，认为人类对屏幕的依赖不会很快消失，并指出从电视到智能手机的例子，说明人们可能更喜欢视觉界面而不是语音交互。他质疑未来穿戴计算设备是否真的能如某些思想领袖所预测的那样融入生活。
• [rimeice的观点] 认为语音界面可以像其他工具的快捷键一样，通过学习特定词汇和组合来实现高效操作。他提到未来可能会有统一的语音指令标准来完成常见任务。
• [nottorp的观点] 对高度自动化的计算机关系表示怀疑，指出即使经过长时间的磨合，人类之间的默契也难以完全自动化，质疑计算机能否在新的任务上准确猜测用户意图。
• [randomfool的观点] 以当前讨论在一个线程对话中进行为例，间接回应了对语音UI的讨论。
• [anthk的观点] 认为物理键盘是更高效的输入工具，不推荐使用智能手机进行打字。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于语音UI的效率是否能达到或超越传统视觉界面和键盘输入，特别是在复杂任务和多任务处理中的表现。
• 讨论中还涉及到语言的自动压缩现象，以及语音UI在特定场景下的潜在优势和局限。
• 有人对未来穿戴计算设备和语音UI的普及持怀疑态度，认为屏幕和视觉界面在短期内不会消失。
